noble_sons_crime.title: A Noble Son's Crime
noble_sons_crime.text: {name2}, the son of a landed family, killed a tanner of {settlement} in a drunken quarrel. Witnesses abound. His father begs mercy and hints at gratitude; the tanner's widow demands the rope.

ignore.result: You let it rot. The commons say the gallows are only for the poor.

choices.label: Hang him — the law is the same for all
choices.result: {name2} hangs at dawn. The commons cheer; the great families mark the day.
choices.chronicle: {house} hanged a noble's son for murder in {settlement}.

choices.label: Exact a blood-price for the widow
choices.result: The father pays the widow handsomely. No one is happy, which is how justice often feels.

choices.label: Accept the father's 'gratitude'
choices.result: The purse is heavy and the boy walks free.

choices.label: Pardon him for his family's service
choices.result: {name2} walks free with a lecture. The widow's curses follow you up the stairs.

refugees_at_gates.title: Refugees at the Gates
refugees_at_gates.text: Hundreds of refugees fleeing war have gathered outside {settlement}. Their spokeswoman, {name}, asks for shelter. The townsfolk eye them warily.

ignore.result: The refugees camped at the walls until hunger and fever broke them up.

choices.label: Open the gates
choices.result: The refugees stream in, thin and grateful.

choices.label: Admit those who will serve in the militia
choices.result: The able-bodied take up spears; the rest move on.

choices.label: Turn them away
choices.result: The gates stay shut. The column trudges on down the road.

migrants_seek_land.title: Settlers Seek Land
migrants_seek_land.text: A band of landless families led by {name} asks leave to clear the woods beside {settlement} and settle there under your protection.

ignore.result: The families moved on to a kinder lord.

choices.label: Grant them the woodland, tax-free for a year
choices.result: Axes ring in the woods by {settlement}.

choices.label: Grant it, for rent
choices.result: They agree to your terms, without enthusiasm.

choices.label: The woods are for your hunting
choices.result: The families leave. The deer remain.

peoples_conflict.title: Quarrel of the Quarters
peoples_conflict.text: In {settlement}, the {people} and the {rivalPeople} have come to blows over the market well. Elders of both peoples stand before you, each demanding the other be punished.

ignore.result: The quarters settled it themselves, with cudgels.

choices.label: Side with the {people}
choices.result: The {people} rejoice. The {rivalPeople} will not forget.

choices.label: Side with the {rivalPeople}
choices.result: The {rivalPeople} rejoice. The {people} will not forget.

choices.label: Dig a second well for all
choices.result: Two wells, and a fragile peace.

choices.label: Flog the brawlers of both quarters
choices.result: Order returns at the end of a whip.

peoples_festival_ban.title: A Foreign Rite
peoples_festival_ban.text: The {people} of {settlement} wish to hold their ancestral rite in the streets. Townsfolk call it strange and unlucky, and {name} has gathered signatures to ban it.

ignore.result: The rite went ahead amid jeers and thrown stones.

choices.label: Allow the rite, under the watch's protection
choices.result: Drums and masks fill the streets. Some townsfolk even join in.

choices.label: Ban it within the walls
choices.result: The {people} hold their rite in a field outside, grieving.

choices.label: Attend the rite yourself
choices.result: Your presence silences the jeering. The {people} will speak of it for years.
choices.chronicle: {house} honoured the rites of the {people} at {settlement}.

bandit_surrender.title: The Bandit's Surrender
bandit_surrender.text: {name}, a bandit captain who has plagued the roads near {settlement}, comes under a white flag. He offers to lay down arms — in exchange for a pardon for himself and his men.

ignore.result: Unanswered, the bandits went back to the roads.

choices.label: Pardon him and take his men into your guard
choices.result: {name} kneels and swears to serve. Your sergeants look doubtful.
choices.chronicle: {house} pardoned the bandit {name} and took him into service.

choices.label: Seize and hang him
choices.result: A white flag is no shield for a murderer. {name} hangs at the crossroads.

choices.label: Take his hoard and let him go
choices.result: The bandit's chest is heavy. He rides off lighter, and smiling.

temple_request.title: A Temple for {settlement}
temple_request.text: Father {name} of {faith} asks you to fund a proper temple in {settlement}. The faithful worship in a barn, he says, and the gods notice such things.

ignore.result: The priest preached a sermon on ungrateful lords.

choices.label: Fund a stone temple
choices.result: Masons arrive within the week. The faithful weep at the first stone.

choices.label: Fund a modest shrine
choices.result: A small shrine rises by the well.

choices.label: Demand the priests tithe to you instead
choices.result: Father {name} pays, pale with fury.

choices.label: Refuse politely
choices.result: The priest bows stiffly and leaves.

moneylender_debt.title: The Moneylender's Bond
moneylender_debt.text: {name2}, a moneylender of {settlement}, holds the bond of {name}, a cooper who cannot pay. By the letter of the contract the cooper's house and tools are forfeit.

ignore.result: The moneylender took the cooper's house. The town took note.

choices.label: Enforce the contract
choices.result: A bond is a bond. The cooper's family moves in with his sister.

choices.label: Cancel the debt by decree
choices.result: The moneylender tears the bond with shaking hands.

choices.label: Pay half from your purse and reschedule the rest
choices.result: Both men leave with something. The town admires the compromise.

choices.label: Cap interest across the town
choices.result: Your decree is read in the square. The lenders draw up new contracts.

widow_inheritance.title: The Widow's Forge
widow_inheritance.text: The smith of {settlement} has died. His widow, {name}, means to keep the forge. His brother, {name2}, says custom gives it to him.

ignore.result: The brother took the forge by force; the widow took to the road.

choices.label: The forge is the widow's
choices.result: {name} relights the forge the same night.

choices.label: Custom gives it to the brother
choices.result: Custom is satisfied. The widow is not.

choices.label: Sell the forge and split the price (less your fee)
choices.result: A new smith buys the forge. The family splits the coin and the grudge.

soldiers_tavern_brawl.title: Soldiers Wreck a Tavern
soldiers_tavern_brawl.text: Men of the garrison smashed {name}'s tavern in {settlement} after a dispute over a dice game. The tavernkeeper wants compensation; the sergeant says his men were cheated.

ignore.result: The tavern stays shuttered and the soldiers swagger.

choices.label: Dock the soldiers' pay
choices.result: The men pay, and mutter.

choices.label: Pay from the treasury
choices.result: The tavern reopens. The soldiers learn nothing.

choices.label: Flog the ringleaders
choices.result: Discipline is restored, publicly.

witch_accusation.title: The Herbwoman Accused
witch_accusation.text: A child in {settlement} has sickened, and the mob blames {name}, an old herbwoman who lives by the mill. They drag her before you crying witchcraft.

ignore.result: Left to itself, the mob decided. It was ugly.

choices.label: Take her under your protection
choices.result: The mob disperses, sullen. {name} bows deeply to you.

choices.label: Banish her from the town
choices.result: {name} hobbles away down the north road.

choices.label: Hold a proper trial

success.result: The physician shows the child ate bad mushrooms. The town is shamed and quiet.

failure.result: The trial finds nothing either way. Nobody is satisfied.

choices.result: You summon witnesses and a physician.

miners_strike.title: The Miners Lay Down Picks
miners_strike.text: The miners and quarrymen of {settlement} refuse to work. {name} speaks for them: the pay is a pittance and the tunnels kill a man a month.

ignore.result: The strike dragged on; the town went without stone and ore.

choices.label: Raise their wages from your treasury
choices.result: The picks ring again.

choices.label: Promise a share of next season's profit
choices.result: The miners return to work on your word.

choices.label: Break the strike with the garrison
choices.result: Spears drive the miners back into the dark.

deserter_caught.title: A Deserter Caught
deserter_caught.text: {name}, a young levy, ran from the war and was caught hiding in his mother's barn near {settlement}. The captains want an example made.

ignore.result: The captains carried out the sentence themselves, and despised you for not giving it.

choices.label: Hang him as an example
choices.result: The levies watch {name} hang. None desert that month.

choices.label: Send him back to the front lines
choices.result: {name} returns to the line under guard.

choices.label: Spare him — he is a boy
choices.result: His mother kisses your boots. The captains mutter about softness.

war_levy_plea.title: Spare Us the Levy
war_levy_plea.text: With the harvest standing, the people of {settlement} beg exemption from the war levy. {name} says if the men march, the grain will rot.

ignore.result: The levy was taken by default. Half the harvest rotted.

choices.label: Exempt them
choices.result: The men stay to reap. The captains count their thin ranks.

choices.label: The levy stands
choices.result: The men march. The women and old folk reap what they can.

choices.label: Hire mercenaries in their place
choices.result: Hired swords march in place of farmers.

foreign_merchant_rights.title: A Foreign Merchant Prince
foreign_merchant_rights.text: {name}, a merchant prince from distant lands, asks for a warehouse and the right to trade freely in {settlement}, offering a gift of rare spices and silver.

ignore.result: The merchant prince took his caravans elsewhere.

choices.label: Grant him free trade
choices.result: Spices and silks fill the market — and local merchants fume.

choices.label: Grant it, with a heavy toll
choices.result: He accepts, calculating.

choices.label: Protect the local guilds
choices.result: The local guilds toast your name.

monastery_exemption.title: The Abbey's Exemption
monastery_exemption.text: The abbot of a {faith} abbey near {settlement} asks that its lands be freed from tax, that the brothers may feed the poor.

ignore.result: The abbot complains to his superiors of your indifference.

choices.label: Grant the exemption
choices.result: The abbey's bells ring in your honour.

choices.label: Tax them like anyone else
choices.result: The abbot pays, and prays for your soul with feeling.

choices.label: Exempt them in exchange for a school
choices.result: The brothers will teach the town's children their letters.

orphans.title: The Orphans of {settlement}
orphans.text: Fever has left a dozen children orphaned in {settlement}. {name}, a washerwoman, has been feeding them from her own pot, and begs for help.

ignore.result: The children scattered to the streets.

choices.label: Found an orphanage
choices.result: A house with a hearth and a matron. The children have a home.

choices.label: Give them to the temple's care
choices.result: The priests take them in.

choices.label: Bind them as apprentices
choices.result: The guilds get cheap hands; the children get a trade, eventually.

poacher.title: The Poacher
poacher.text: Your foresters have caught {name} with a deer on his shoulders. His family is starving, he says, and he had no other way.

ignore.result: The foresters let him go, and the woods filled with snares.

choices.label: Hang him by forest law
choices.result: Forest law is old and hard. {name} hangs.

choices.label: Fine him and keep the deer
choices.result: He pays what he has.

choices.label: Hire him as a gamekeeper
choices.result: Who better to catch poachers than a poacher?

festival_request.title: A Midsummer Feast
festival_request.text: The folk of {settlement} ask you to sponsor the midsummer feast — oxen, ale, musicians — as the old lords did.

ignore.result: The feast was a meagre affair, and they knew whom to blame.

choices.label: Sponsor a lavish feast
choices.result: The ale flows for three days. Songs are made about your table.

choices.label: Sponsor a modest feast
choices.result: Bread, beer and a fiddler. It suffices.

choices.label: Times are hard; no feast this year
choices.result: The square stays quiet on midsummer night.

disputed_match.title: A Match Across a Feud
disputed_match.text: {name}, the daughter of a family sworn to {house}, wishes to marry a son of {rival}. Her father asks whether the House forbids it.

ignore.result: The lovers eloped. Both houses took offence.

choices.label: Bless the match
choices.result: A wedding softens old grudges — a little.
choices.chronicle: {house} blessed a marriage with {rival}, cooling an old feud.

choices.label: Forbid it
choices.result: The girl weeps; her father thanks you.

choices.label: Bless it, and demand a dowry from {rival}
choices.result: {rival} pays, with very bad grace.

cousin_debts.title: The Cousin's Debts
cousin_debts.text: {name}, a cousin of {house}, has run up ruinous gambling debts in the name of the House. His creditors are at your door.

ignore.result: The creditors spread word that {house} does not pay its debts.

choices.label: Pay the debts — the House's name is at stake
choices.result: The creditors are paid. {name} is lectured within an inch of his life.

choices.label: Disown him publicly
choices.result: {name} is struck from the House's rolls.

choices.label: Make him work the debt off in your service
choices.result: {name} becomes the House's least willing clerk.

rival_herald_insult.title: A Herald's Insult
rival_herald_insult.text: A herald of {rival} has read out a mocking verse about {house} in the great hall of {kingdom}. Your household waits to see how you answer.

ignore.result: Silence was taken for weakness.

choices.label: Demand a public apology
choices.result: {rival} apologizes through gritted teeth.

choices.label: Laugh it off
choices.result: Your good humour wins some admirers — and some sneers.

choices.label: Answer with a sharper verse

success.result: Your reply is repeated in every tavern. {rival} is the joke now.

failure.result: Your verse limps. The court winces.

choices.result: You call for pen and ink.

veterans_pension.title: The Old Soldiers
veterans_pension.text: Grey veterans of old campaigns, led by {name}, ask for pensions. They bled for the realm, they say, and now beg in the streets of {settlement}.

ignore.result: The veterans told every recruit how the realm repays its soldiers.

choices.label: Grant pensions
choices.result: The old soldiers salute you with shaking hands.

choices.label: Grant them plots of land instead
choices.result: Swords to ploughshares, literally.

choices.label: Refuse — they were paid in their day
choices.result: The veterans spit on the steps as they leave.

plague_quarantine.title: Fever in the Lower Town
plague_quarantine.text: {name}, a physician of {settlement}, warns that a fever is spreading in the lower town. She asks you to seal it off before it reaches the rest.

ignore.result: No action was taken. The fever spread.

choices.label: Seal the lower town
choices.result: Chains go up across the lanes. Behind them, people wail.

choices.label: Pay physicians to treat the sick
choices.result: Physicians in beaked masks go door to door.

choices.label: Leave it to prayer
choices.result: The priests lead processions through the lower town.

smuggler_bribe.title: The Smugglers' Offer
smuggler_bribe.text: A smooth-tongued fellow named {name} offers you a share of the smuggling trade through {settlement} — if your toll-men look the other way.

ignore.result: The smugglers took your silence as consent, and paid you nothing.

choices.label: Take your cut
choices.result: A purse appears on your table every new moon.

choices.label: Arrest him and raid the warehouses
choices.result: Contraband piles up in the square. {name} sits in a cell.

choices.label: Make them pay a legal toll
choices.result: Smugglers become importers, at a price.

pilgrim_shelter.title: Pilgrims Seek Shelter
pilgrim_shelter.text: A column of {faith} pilgrims led by {name} asks for food and shelter in {settlement} on their way to a holy site.

ignore.result: The pilgrims slept in the ditches and spoke of your town's coldness.

choices.label: Shelter and feed them
choices.result: The pilgrims bless your hall as they go.

choices.label: Charge them for lodging
choices.result: Pilgrims pay; pilgrims remember.

choices.label: Walk a day's road with them
choices.result: Your company on the road inspires several to take up your faith.

council_seat.title: A Seat on the Council
council_seat.text: {name}, a wealthy burgher of {kingdom}, asks you to name him to the council. He promises the guilds' support — and a handsome gift.

ignore.result: The burgher found a more obliging patron.

choices.label: Appoint him
choices.result: The nobles are appalled to sit beside a draper.

choices.label: Council seats are not for sale
choices.result: The burgher leaves with his purse.

choices.label: Offer the seat to a commoner instead
choices.result: A blacksmith sits on the council. The realm talks of nothing else.
choices.chronicle: {house} gave a council seat in {kingdom} to a commoner.

border_lord_tribute.title: The Border Lord's Grievance
border_lord_tribute.text: {name}, a lord on the marches of {kingdom}, complains that royal taxes leave him nothing to pay his garrison. He hints that the realm's enemies pay better.

ignore.result: The border lord grew sullen, and his gates less watchful.

choices.label: Remit his taxes for a year
choices.result: The marches hold firm.

choices.label: Remind him what treason costs

failure.result: He opens his gates to raiders out of spite.

choices.result: You send a letter sealed in black wax.

choices.label: Send royal troops to his castle
choices.result: Royal banners fly over the marches.

colony_autonomy.title: The Colonists' Charter
colony_autonomy.text: The elders of {settlement}, led by {name}, ask for a charter of rights: their own council, their own courts, and lower taxes.

ignore.result: The elders read your silence as contempt.

choices.label: Grant the charter
choices.result: {settlement} celebrates its charter.

choices.label: Grant them a council, but keep the courts
choices.result: Half a loaf, accepted gravely.

choices.label: Refuse — a colony is ruled, not consulted
choices.result: The elders leave in silence.

bandit_loyal.title: The Pardoned Bandit Returns
bandit_loyal.text: {prior}, the bandit you pardoned, has served your guard with ferocious loyalty. Today he brings in the heads of the gang he once rode with, and asks for a captain's rank.

ignore.result: {prior} took the silence hard, but stayed.

choices.label: Make him a captain
choices.result: Captain {prior} salutes you. The roads are safer than they have been in years.
choices.chronicle: {prior}, once a bandit pardoned by {house}, became a captain of its guard.

choices.label: Reward him with gold, but no rank
choices.result: {prior} pockets the gold with a shrug.

bandit_betrays.title: The Bandit's Betrayal
bandit_betrays.text: {prior}, the bandit you pardoned, has fled back to the hills — with the guard's horses and the strongbox of {settlement}.

ignore.result: {prior} is a legend in the taverns now — at your expense.

choices.label: Lead the hunt yourself
choices.result: You run {prior} to ground in a shepherd's hut. This time there is no pardon.

choices.label: Post a bounty
choices.result: Bounty hunters bring back his head within the month.

choices.label: Let him go — the lesson is learned
choices.result: The strongbox is gone. So is your faith in reformed men.

bandit_raids_again.title: The Bandit Rides Again
bandit_raids_again.text: {prior}, the bandit you let go with his life for his hoard, has rebuilt his band. Farms near {settlement} are burning.

ignore.result: The raids went on unchecked.

choices.label: Ride out against him
choices.result: His band scatters before your riders.

choices.label: Pay him to go elsewhere
choices.result: He takes the gold — and someone else's farms burn.

noble_son_again.title: He Has Killed Again
noble_son_again.text: {prior}, the noble son you spared, has killed again — a serving girl this time. The town is at the edge of riot, and everyone remembers your last ruling.

ignore.result: A mob burned the young lord's family home. Order broke down for days.

choices.label: Hang him now
choices.result: Too late for the girl. Not too late for justice, the people say — barely.
choices.chronicle: {house} hanged {prior}, twice a killer, too late to save his second victim.

choices.label: Exile him beyond the realm
choices.result: {prior} is put on a ship. The town is not appeased.

choices.label: Protect him again
choices.result: Your guards ring his family's house. Stones fly at your banners.

heretic_flock.title: The Preacher's Flock
heretic_flock.text: {prior}, the hedge preacher you let speak, now has a flock of hundreds in {settlement}. They ask for a chapel of their own; the priests of {faith} call it open heresy.

ignore.result: The flock built its chapel anyway, and the priests blame you.

choices.label: Let them build
choices.result: A plain timber chapel rises. Its bell sounds different from the temple's.

choices.label: Disperse the flock
choices.result: Soldiers break up the meetings. {prior} vanishes into the hills.

choices.label: Invite {prior} into the established temple

success.result: {prior} accepts a pulpit. The schism heals.

choices.result: You broker a meeting between preacher and priests.

refugees_settled.title: The Refugees Give Thanks
refugees_settled.text: The refugees you sheltered in {settlement} have cleared fields and raised houses. {prior} comes with their first harvest as a gift.

ignore.result: The gift went unacknowledged.

choices.label: Accept their gift
choices.result: Their harvest fills your table.

choices.label: Return it — let them keep their first harvest
choices.result: They will tell their grandchildren of this.
choices.chronicle: The refugees of {settlement} became loyal subjects of {house}.

refugees_unrest.title: Old Townsfolk and New
refugees_unrest.text: The refugees you admitted to {settlement} are clashing with the old townsfolk over work and wages. {prior} says her people are being driven from the market.

ignore.result: The clashes festered into a riot.

choices.label: Guarantee the newcomers' rights
choices.result: The law protects the newcomers. The old townsfolk resent it.

choices.label: Pay for public works to employ them
choices.result: New walls, new jobs, fewer fights.

choices.label: Send the troublemakers away
choices.result: Shelter, it turns out, had conditions.

herbwoman_healer.title: The Herbwoman's Cure
herbwoman_healer.text: {prior}, the herbwoman you protected, has broken a fever that the priests could not. The mothers of {settlement} want her honoured — and the priests want her silenced.

ignore.result: {prior} went back to her hut by the mill.

choices.label: Name her town physician
choices.result: {prior} has a salary now, and a house near the square.
choices.chronicle: {house} named the once-accused herbwoman {prior} physician of {settlement}.

choices.label: Honour her quietly
choices.result: A purse and a word of thanks.

miners_promise.title: The Miners Call in Your Promise
miners_promise.text: {prior} and the miners of {settlement} have worked the season on your word. Now they want the share you promised.

ignore.result: A broken promise. The mines fell silent again.

choices.label: Pay the promised share
choices.result: Your word is good. The miners will work for you again.

choices.label: Renege — profits were poor
choices.result: The miners curse your name in the dark.

gamekeeper_report.title: The Gamekeeper's Catch
gamekeeper_report.text: {prior}, the poacher you made gamekeeper, has broken a ring of poachers selling your deer in three towns. He brings the ringleader to you.

ignore.result: The ringleader bribed his way out.

choices.label: Reward {prior}
choices.result: The poacher-turned-keeper beams with pride.

choices.label: Fine the ring heavily
choices.result: The ring pays for every deer, twice over.

plague_contained.title: The Fever Breaks
plague_contained.text: {prior} reports that the fever in {settlement} has broken. The lower town is mourning, but the rest of the town was spared.

ignore.result: The physicians went unthanked.

choices.label: Reward the physicians
choices.result: {prior} is cheered through the streets.

choices.label: Hold a service of thanksgiving
choices.result: The temple is packed to the doors.

plague_spreads.title: The Fever Spreads
plague_spreads.text: Despite everything, the fever has burst out of the lower town of {settlement}. {prior} begs for drastic measures.

ignore.result: The fever ran its course. The graveyards filled.

choices.label: Burn the infected quarter
choices.result: Smoke hangs over {settlement} for days. The fever dies with the houses.

choices.label: Bring physicians from every town
choices.result: The fever is beaten back, at great cost.

choices.label: Let those who can flee
choices.result: Half the town empties onto the roads.

smuggling_exposed.title: Your Arrangement Exposed
smuggling_exposed.text: A customs clerk has found your name in {prior}'s smuggling ledgers. He has not yet gone to the magistrates.

ignore.result: The clerk went to the magistrates. The ledgers were read aloud.

choices.label: Pay the clerk to burn the ledgers
choices.result: The ledgers burn. The clerk buys a fine house.

choices.label: Confess and pay restitution
choices.result: Your honesty is admired, if not your past.
choices.chronicle: {house} confessed to profiting from smuggling and paid restitution.

choices.label: Deny everything

success.result: The ledgers are dismissed as forgeries.

choices.result: You meet the accusation with a stony face.

guild_overreach.title: The Guild Squeezes the Town
guild_overreach.text: The clothiers' guild you granted a monopoly in {settlement} has tripled the price of cloth. {prior}'s guild is rich; the town shivers.

ignore.result: The guild kept squeezing.

choices.label: Revoke the monopoly
choices.result: The peddlers return. The guild masters are livid.

choices.label: Tax their windfall
choices.result: If the guild must be rich, the crown will share it.

choices.label: A charter is a charter
choices.result: The guild thanks you. The town does not.

usury_backlash.title: The Lenders Close Their Doors
usury_backlash.text: Since your cap on interest, the moneylenders of {settlement} — {prior} among them — refuse to lend at all. Farmers cannot buy seed.

ignore.result: Fields lay unsown for want of credit.

choices.label: Lend seed money from your own treasury
choices.result: The crown becomes the town's banker.

choices.label: Repeal the cap
choices.result: The lenders reopen, smug.

choices.label: Order them to lend
choices.result: They lend, grudgingly, and badly.

cousin_revenge.title: The Disowned Cousin
cousin_revenge.text: {prior}, the cousin you disowned, has turned up at the court of {rival}, telling everyone who will listen the secrets of {house}.

ignore.result: {prior}'s stories spread unchallenged.

choices.label: Buy his silence and his return
choices.result: {prior} slinks home, chastened and richer.

choices.label: Denounce him as a liar
choices.result: A war of words. Neither side wins.

choices.label: Let {rival} keep him
choices.result: Let them have the fool.

royal_succession_worries.title: Who Comes After?
royal_succession_worries.text: The great lords of {kingdom} gather in the hall, and {name}, the eldest of them, speaks for all: the realm worries for the succession. Will the crown name its heir before the lords and swear them to it?

ignore.result: The question hangs unanswered over the court, and the lords draw their own conclusions.

choices.label: Have every lord swear to your heir
choices.result: One by one the lords kneel and swear. The realm breathes easier.

choices.label: Answer with a feast for the heir
choices.result: The heir is toasted until dawn. The lords go home well fed and reassured.

choices.label: The succession is the crown's affair
choices.result: The lords bow stiffly and say no more — aloud.

royal_foreign_envoy.title: An Envoy from {rivalRealm}
royal_foreign_envoy.text: An envoy of {rivalRealm} presents himself at court with a scroll of grievances: old border raids, slights to his master's honour. He hints that gold would soothe them — and that a refusal will be remembered.

ignore.result: The envoy left unheard. {rivalRealm} takes it as an insult.

choices.label: Pay for peace (400g from the treasury)
choices.result: The envoy departs mollified. Your lords mutter that the crown buys its peace.

choices.label: Refuse with courtesy
choices.result: The envoy bows and leaves. Nothing is settled, but nothing is lost.

choices.label: Send him home without his beard
choices.result: The court roars with laughter. {rivalRealm} will not.

royal_alliance_offer.title: A Pact Offered by {friendRealm}
royal_alliance_offer.text: Envoys of {friendRealm} bring gifts and a proposal: a closer friendship between the two crowns, sealed with royal favour on both sides.

ignore.result: The envoys tired of waiting and sailed home.

choices.label: Embrace the friendship (gifts in return)
choices.result: Gifts are exchanged and toasts drunk. The two crowns draw closer.

choices.label: Thank them, promise nothing
choices.result: Warm words, no oaths. {friendRealm} hoped for more.

choices.label: The crown needs no friends
choices.result: The envoys leave cold. Your lords admire the pride; your merchants less so.

royal_border_dispute.title: A Border Dispute with {rivalRealm}
royal_border_dispute.text: Shepherds of {rivalRealm} graze a disputed valley on the march, and their lord has raised a tower there. Your marcher lords demand you answer it.

ignore.result: The tower stands, and your marcher lords think their king weak.

choices.label: Send the royal host to tear it down
choices.result: The tower comes down and the valley is yours. {rivalRealm} seethes.

choices.label: Pay jurists to argue the old charters
choices.result: The jurists find for you on paper. The tower is quietly abandoned.

choices.label: Let them have the valley
choices.result: Peace on the march — and a grievance in every marcher hall.

royal_plague.title: Plague in {settlement}
royal_plague.text: The sweating sickness has reached the capital. Physicians beg for a quarantine of the lower town; the guilds beg you not to close the markets.

ignore.result: The sickness ran its course through the crowded streets.

choices.label: Close the lower town (300g)
choices.result: The cordon holds. The dead are few; the merchants count their losses.

choices.label: Order processions and prayers
choices.result: The faithful pray in the streets. The sickness takes its toll regardless.

choices.label: The court withdraws to the country
choices.result: The court is safe. The capital does not forget who left it.

royal_levy_remission.title: The Lords Plead Poverty
royal_levy_remission.text: After a hard season, {name} speaks for the lesser lords: their tenants cannot meet the royal dues. They beg a remission of this year's levy.

ignore.result: The dues were collected by force, and the lords remember it.

choices.label: Remit the dues (−400 treasury)
choices.result: The lords go home blessing your name.

choices.label: Remit half
choices.result: A fair middle, grudgingly accepted.

choices.label: The dues are the dues
choices.result: The crown's collectors ride out. The lords pay, and resent it.

royal_veterans.title: The Veterans' Arrears
royal_veterans.text: Old soldiers of the royal host crowd the palace gate: they were promised pay and land after the last campaign and have seen neither.

ignore.result: The veterans dispersed — some to the taverns, some to the hills as bandits.

choices.label: Pay their arrears (350g)
choices.result: Paid and proud, many re-enlist on the spot.

choices.label: Settle them on crown land
choices.result: The veterans take up the plough. The lords grumble at the crown's generosity with land.

choices.label: Have the guard disperse them
choices.result: The gate is cleared. The army hears of it.

royal_tournament.title: A Royal Tournament
royal_tournament.text: {name}, master of the royal lists, proposes a great tournament in honour of the crown: every lord's champion would ride, and the realm would talk of nothing else for a season.

ignore.result: The lists stay empty this year.

choices.label: A grand tournament (500g)
choices.result: Banners, lances and feasting for a week. The lords will speak of it for years.

choices.label: A modest one (200g)
choices.result: A fine day of jousting, soon forgotten.

choices.label: The treasury has better uses
choices.result: The master of the lists sulks. The steward approves.

companions._comment: Companions with a life of their own (src/systems/companions.js). Values decide how a travel companion's approval reacts to the player's deeds (Traits deed counters and earned traits), court rulings (petition court axes), quest-stat events (piracy, conquest, pilgrimage…), karma swings and battles. Approval tiers scale the companion's bonus; low approval brings gripes, raise demands, desertion and — rarely, after a warning — betrayal. High approval unlocks a personal quest (templates below); finishing it makes the companion devoted with a permanent perk. Personalities are generated deterministically from a hash of the companion's id.

honour: "That was done rightly. I'm proud to ride with you."
"Honour still means something on this road."
piety: "A blessed deed. I'll light a candle for it."
greed: "Now that's the kind of business I like."
"Coin in the purse — a good day."
compassion: "You have a kind heart. Don't let the road harden it."
"People will sleep easier tonight because of you."
ambition: "Keep this up and they'll sing of us."
freedom: "Open roads and free folk — this is living."
loyalty_kingdom: "My homeland would thank you for that."
"You've been a friend to my people."

honour: "I didn't swear to follow a liar and a coward."
"There's no honour in that, and you know it."
piety: "The gods turn their faces from such things."
"I'll be praying for your soul tonight."
greed: "Generosity is a fine word for waste."
compassion: "Those were people. Do you even remember their faces?"
"I can't keep looking away from what you do."
ambition: "We ran. We RAN. Do you know what that costs a name?"
freedom: "Chains and tithes and iron rule. I didn't come for this."
"Every gate you shut is one more cage."
loyalty_kingdom: "You've made enemies of my own people."
"My homeland won't forget this — and neither will I."
loyalty_faith: "You mock the faith with every step."
"The temple would be ashamed of you."

battleWin: "Another day we live. Drinks are on you."
battleLoss: "That was a slaughter. We need a better plan."
"I've seen better days — and better commanders."
unpaid: "Where's my wage? A promise doesn't fill a belly."
"No coin again. My patience has a bottom, you know."
complain: "We need to talk about how things are going."
"Don't think I haven't noticed what you've been doing."
talkHappy: "Glad to be on the road with you."
"Tell me another story of the old days."
talkContent: "The road's long, but the company's decent."
gift: "You didn't have to. But I'm glad you did."
warning: {name} has been counting your purse with an odd look, and was seen talking quietly with strangers at the last inn.

pathfinder.name: Pathfinder
pathfinder.text: +3% battle power, heals 1 more a day

avenge_family.title: Blood Owed
avenge_family.description: {name}'s {kin} was cut down by {foe}'s band years ago. {name} has never forgotten. Help them bring the killers to the sword.
avenge_family.chronicle: {name} avenged their {kin} at {player}'s side and swore their blade to the House forever.

lost_sibling.title: The Lost {kinTitle}
lost_sibling.description: {name}'s {kin} vanished on the trade roads long ago. Rumour says they were seen in a distant town. Ask in taverns and search the settlements.
lost_sibling.chronicle: {name} found their lost {kin} at last, and named {player} family for it.

clear_debt.title: A Debt Come Due
clear_debt.description: {name} owes 300 gold to a moneylender who has threatened their family. Help them pay it off (from the companion roster) before the interest swallows them.
clear_debt.chronicle: {player} paid off {name}'s ruinous debt; {name} has kept the House's ledgers faithfully ever since.

pilgrimage.title: The Long Pilgrimage
pilgrimage.description: {name} made a vow at their {kin}'s deathbed to walk to the holy places. Walk it with them.

heirloom.title: {heirloomTitle}
heirloom.description: {name}'s family lost {heirloom} when raiders looted their home; it was last traced to the old ruins. Delve the ruins and recover it.
heirloom.chronicle: {player} recovered {heirloom} from the ruins and returned it to {name}.

slay_beast.title: The Beast of the Hills
slay_beast.description: A monster savaged {name}'s home village and took their {kin}. {name} wants it dead.
slay_beast.chronicle: {name} watched the beast that took their {kin} fall to {player}'s spear.

family_fortune.title: Restore the Family House
family_fortune.description: {name}'s family trading house was ruined by a rival. Make enough in trade to set them back on their feet.
family_fortune.chronicle: With {player}'s help, {name} restored their family's trading house.

taken_at_sea.title: Taken at Sea
taken_at_sea.description: Pirates under {foe} took {name}'s {kin} and their ship. {name} wants the sea-wolves made to pay.
taken_at_sea.chronicle: {name} saw {foe}'s pirates broken on the waves, at {player}'s command.

stolen_manuscript.title: The Stolen Manuscript
stolen_manuscript.description: {name}'s life's work was stolen by a rival scholar and hidden away. Hire an informant to learn where, then retrieve it from the old ruins.

objectives.text: Hire an informant to trace the thief
Recover the manuscript from the ruins

stolen_manuscript.chronicle: {player} recovered {name}'s stolen manuscript; its pages now carry the House's name.

clear_name.title: A Name Cleared
clear_name.description: {name} was branded a raider by {foe}, whose own band burns the borderlands. Drive the real raiders off and clear {name}'s name.
clear_name.chronicle: {name}'s name was cleared when {player} broke {foe}'s raiders.

healers_oath.title: The Healer's Oath
healers_oath.description: {name} swore to tend the sick of a plague-struck town where their {kin} died. Give generously and help them keep the oath.

objectives.text: Give 150 gold of charity through {name} (companion roster)

healers_oath.chronicle: {name} kept their healer's oath with {player}'s purse behind them.

sunken.name: Sunken Ruins
sunken.intro: The old city settled into the mire long ago. Stairs vanish into black water, and the halls below breathe a cold, wet air.

tomb.name: Buried Tomb
tomb.intro: Beneath the broken stones a stair descends into a barrow of the old kings. The air is dry and tastes of dust and resin.

ruins.name: Ancient Ruins
ruins.intro: Past the fallen gate, the cellars of the old kingdom still run deep beneath the rubble — halls, vaults and stairs no one has walked in centuries.

mine.name: Abandoned Mine
mine.intro: Rotten timbers prop the mouth of an old mine. Rails run down into the dark, and somewhere below, water drips onto stone.

cave.name: Deep Cave
cave.intro: The cave mouth narrows, then opens into passages that wind far deeper than any shepherd has dared to go.

collapsed_hall.name: Collapsed Hall
collapsed_hall.text: Half the ceiling lies across the floor. Beyond the rubble you glimpse the glint of something left behind.

success.text: Stone by stone you clear a path to a forgotten strongbox.

failure.text: A slab shifts and pins your leg before you wrench free.

success.text: You wriggle through and find a purse in a dead man's hand.

failure.text: Loose stone rains down as you crawl.

trapped_corridor.name: Trapped Corridor
trapped_corridor.text: Flagstones in a long corridor sit a hair too proud of the floor. Dark holes line the walls at chest height.

success.text: The mechanism clicks dead. Its bronze darts are worth keeping.

failure.text: A dart grazes your neck. The poison burns.

success.text: Darts rattle off your guard as you charge the length of the hall.

failure.text: You run the gauntlet and pay for every step.

inscription_wall.name: The Inscribed Wall
inscription_wall.text: A wall dense with carved script — names, dates, perhaps a warning. Some of the glyphs are the sigils of a forgotten god.

choices.label: Read the inscription
choices.hint: Intelligence and cartography. Learn what lies ahead.

success.text: The words map the halls below and name the dead who sleep there.

failure.text: The script defeats you, and the hours slip away.

success.text: The sigils blacken and the air lightens. Something here is grateful.

failure.text: The smoke chokes you, and the old god's anger lingers.

success.text: You pass the wall without a second look.

stone_guardian.name: The Watching Statue
stone_guardian.text: A stone warrior stands across the passage, sword grounded. Its eyes are gems, and they seem to follow you.

success.text: You slip by. The statue never stirs.

failure.text: Grit crunches under your boot. The statue's blade swings down.

choices.label: Topple it and take the gem eyes
choices.hint: Strength and combat. Rich, if you win.

success.text: The guardian shatters. You pry out its eyes.

failure.text: It does not shatter. It wakes, and it follows you out of the dark.

treasury_vault.name: The Old Treasury
treasury_vault.text: A vault door of black iron, its lock crusted but whole. Coins have spilled out from beneath it.

success.text: The lock yields. Inside: coin of a dead kingdom.

failure.text: The pick snaps off inside the lock. You gather the spilled coins and nothing more.

success.text: The door crashes in. The hoard is yours.

failure.text: The racket brings the roof down around you.

armory.name: Forgotten Armory
armory.text: Racks of spears and blades line the walls. Most are rust, but not all.

choices.label: Haul out the best of it

success.text: Good steel under the grime.

failure.text: A rack collapses on you.

success.text: Wrapped in oilcloth: a blade etched with runes that still glow faintly.

failure.text: Nothing but rust and a few usable shields.

quiet_alcove.name: A Quiet Alcove
quiet_alcove.text: A dry niche off the passage, out of the draught. It would be a good place to catch your breath — if nothing else thinks so too.

choices.label: Rest here a while
choices.hint: Recover stamina and health. Something may find you.

success.text: You rest undisturbed and bind your hurts.

failure.text: Something with too many legs finds you dozing.

success.text: You press on into the dark.

bandit_hideout.name: Bandits' Hideout
bandit_hideout.text: Firelight. A handful of outlaws have made a den of these halls, and their loot is piled in the corner.

choices.label: Fall on them
choices.hint: Combat. Their stash is yours if you win.

success.text: The outlaws flee or fall. Their stash is yours.

failure.text: They beat you back and you escape bloodied.

choices.label: Talk your way to a share

success.text: They take you for a kindred spirit and share both fire and plunder.

failure.text: They take your purse and show you the way on with a boot.

choices.label: Steal from the pile while they sleep

success.text: You lift the best of their loot unseen.

failure.text: A sentry wakes. Knives in the dark.

ancestor_shrine.name: Shrine of the Ancestors
ancestor_shrine.text: Votive jars and tarnished offerings crowd a low altar to the honored dead.

success.text: A breath of warm air passes over you. The way ahead seems clearer.

choices.label: Take the offerings
choices.hint: Easy coin. The dead may object.

success.text: You sweep the offerings into your pack. Nothing stirs.

failure.text: Something follows you out of the shrine — a weight in your pack that was not there before.

sealed_door.name: The Riddle Door
sealed_door.text: A round stone door sealed by a ring of turning dials, each carved with a different star.

success.text: The stars align and the door rolls aside onto a scholar's cell.

failure.text: A wrong turn, and a gout of foul air leaves you retching.

success.text: The mechanism gives with a shriek. The cell beyond is half-crushed, but there is something.

failure.text: You exhaust yourself on unmoving stone.

bone_pit.name: The Parting of Ways
bone_pit.text: The passage splits. From one way comes a cool draught; the other is strewn with old bones that lead downward.

success.text: The draught leads to a forgotten side passage and a cache within.

failure.text: The draught comes from a crack you can't follow. You lose your way for hours.

choices.label: Follow the bones
choices.hint: Faith and nerve. The dead went somewhere.

success.text: The bones lead to an ossuary where the dead were buried with their wealth.

failure.text: The bones lead to whatever killed them.

sarcophagus_hall.name: Hall of Sarcophagi
sarcophagus_hall.text: A dozen stone coffins rest in a row, their lids carved with the faces of the dead.

choices.label: Prise open the sarcophagi
choices.hint: Strength. Grave goods — and the risk of a curse.

success.text: Gold rings, a gem-set circlet, and dust.

failure.text: The lid slips and the thing inside is not quite dead enough.

choices.label: Pray for the dead
choices.hint: Faith. Piety has its own rewards.

success.text: A peace settles on the hall. A grave-gift lies uncovered where none was before.

failure.text: Your prayers echo hollow. You feel watched.

embalmers_chamber.name: Embalmers' Chamber
embalmers_chamber.text: Shelves of sealed jars, bundles of dried herbs, and the sweet reek of old resins.

success.text: Precious resins and herbs no living garden grows.

failure.text: One jar breathes out a choking dust.

choices.label: Mix a salve from what's here

success.text: The old remedies still work.

failure.text: The mixture stings but does little.

false_tomb.name: The False Tomb
false_tomb.text: A grand tomb, ostentatiously empty. Grave robbers came and went. But the proportions of the room are wrong.

success.text: Behind a false wall lies the true burial, untouched.

failure.text: You tap stone for hours and find only stone.

success.text: The wall crumbles onto a hidden burial.

failure.text: The wrong wall. The ceiling sags ominously.

flooded_gallery.name: Flooded Gallery
flooded_gallery.text: Black water fills the gallery to the shoulder. Through it, the far arch gleams with something gilded.

success.text: You haul yourself out beside a gilded votive cup.

failure.text: The cold steals your breath, and something brushes your leg.

success.text: A crawlway above the waterline leads you around — and past an old offering niche.

failure.text: Every way round ends in water.

drowned_chapel.name: The Drowned Chapel
drowned_chapel.text: A chapel half-sunk in silt. The altar stands above the water; the reliquary lies beneath it.

success.text: Your fingers close on a silver casket.

failure.text: The silt grips you and you surface gasping.

success.text: The water stills. You feel washed clean.

failure.text: Only the drip of water answers.

eel_den.name: The Eel Den
eel_den.text: Something long and slick moves in the pool across your path. Many somethings.

success.text: You cut them down and wade on with supper.

failure.text: Teeth, and more teeth.

success.text: They never notice you.

failure.text: You slip into the pool.

success.text: They boil around the offering while you pass.

rotting_bridge.name: The Rotting Bridge
rotting_bridge.text: A timber walkway spans a dark drop. Half its planks are gone, and the rest are soft.

success.text: Planks crack behind you, but you're across.

failure.text: A plank gives way and you catch the edge, barely.

success.text: Lashed and braced, the bridge holds. On the far side, an old pack.

failure.text: Your work holds, mostly.

silt_chest.name: The Silted Chest
silt_chest.text: The corner of an iron-bound chest juts from the silt, its lock long rusted away.

success.text: It comes free with a sucking groan, heavy with coin.

failure.text: The lid tears off and the contents spill into the mud. You save a little.

success.text: Everything inside survives: coins, glass beads, a sealed letter.

failure.text: The silt slumps back as fast as you dig.

sunken_market.name: The Sunken Market
sunken_market.text: Stalls stand in rows beneath the mire, their awnings long rotted. Merchants left in a hurry.

success.text: Fine glass, spices sealed in wax, a merchant's strongbox.

failure.text: Rot and ruin, but a few coins.

success.text: The guild's ledgers name trade routes and caches long forgotten.

failure.text: The ledgers have turned to pulp.

underground_river.name: The Underground River
underground_river.text: A black river roars through the cavern, and a cool draught blows downstream.

choices.label: Follow the draught along the bank

success.text: The draught leads to a ledge where someone once camped — and charted these tunnels.

failure.text: The bank peters out into sheer rock.

success.text: The river spits you out deep below, beside a glittering shelf.

failure.text: The river batters you against the rocks.

echoing_cavern.name: The Echoing Cavern
echoing_cavern.text: A cavern so vast your torchlight finds no ceiling. Every sound returns a hundredfold.

choices.label: Shout, and map it by the echoes

success.text: The echoes trace the cavern's shape, and you mark it carefully.

failure.text: The echoes wake the bats — and something larger.

success.text: You cross unheard and find a shelf of old offerings.

failure.text: A stumble, and the cavern roars it back.

crystal_grotto.name: Crystal Grotto
crystal_grotto.text: The walls glitter with crystal growths, some as long as your arm.

choices.label: Mine the crystals
choices.hint: Strength; tools help. The roof may not like it.

success.text: You chip free clusters of fine crystal.

failure.text: Crystal and stone come down together.

success.text: A few loose crystals, and a moment of wonder.

bat_roost.name: The Bat Roost
bat_roost.text: The ceiling seethes with bats. The floor beneath is a reeking slope of guano.

success.text: A storm of wings, and you're through.

failure.text: You fall in the muck amid a thousand bites.

success.text: In the dark you find a dead explorer's pack.

failure.text: Blind, you stumble into a crevice.

beast_lair.name: The Beast's Lair
beast_lair.text: Gnawed bones, a musky stink, and the rumble of something big breathing in the dark.

success.text: The beast falls. Its pelt is magnificent.

failure.text: Claws open your arm to the bone.

success.text: It never wakes.

failure.text: One eye opens.

success.text: It eats, and lets you pass.

fungus_garden.name: The Fungus Garden
fungus_garden.text: Pale fungi grow in tiers from the cavern floor, glowing faintly.

choices.label: Harvest the fungi
choices.hint: Intelligence. Some are precious; some are deadly.

success.text: Rare caps for any apothecary.

failure.text: A puffball bursts in your face.

success.text: The fungi blacken and you pass.

old_shaft.name: The Old Shaft
old_shaft.text: A vertical shaft drops into the dark, its ladder long rotted. Far below, something glints.

choices.label: Climb down
choices.hint: Strength; rope helps a great deal.

success.text: At the bottom: a miner's last bag of nuggets.

failure.text: You fall the last stretch.

choices.label: Lower a light and look first

success.text: The light shows a safer gallery beyond the shaft.

failure.text: The light gutters and falls. You learn nothing.

firedamp_gallery.name: Firedamp Gallery
firedamp_gallery.text: The air here smells sweet and wrong. Old miners called it firedamp: one spark and the gallery burns.

choices.label: Douse your light and feel your way
choices.hint: Stealth and intelligence. Slow and blind.

success.text: Groping in the dark, you find an abandoned toolbox.

failure.text: You crack your head on a low beam.

choices.label: Hurry through with the torch
choices.hint: Luck. Very fast, or very bad.

success.text: The flame flickers blue, but holds. You are through.

failure.text: A whump of blue fire. You come to, singed and smoking.

ore_vein.name: The Untouched Vein
ore_vein.text: A seam of rich ore, abandoned when the miners fled. Their picks still lie where they dropped them.

success.text: A good day's haul.

failure.text: Bruising work for a meager pile.

success.text: A pocketful of the best pieces.

miners_ghost.name: The Restless Shade
miners_ghost.text: A pale figure stands in the passage, repeating the motions of some task it can never finish.

success.text: It tells you where it hid its wages, and fades in peace.

failure.text: It shrieks, and its cold passes through you.

success.text: With a word and a gesture, the shade is gone.

failure.text: It does not go. It follows.

cart_track.name: The Ore-Cart Track
cart_track.text: Rails dive steeply downward. An ore cart sits at the top, its wheels still free.

success.text: You rattle down into the depths in moments, laughing.

failure.text: The cart jumps the rails.

success.text: A long walk down. Along the way, a few dropped lumps of coal.

drowned_throne.name: The Drowned Throne
drowned_throne.text: The deepest hall: a throne room beneath the water's skin. On the throne sits a crowned skeleton, and around it, the treasure of a sunken court.

choices.label: Claim the crown
choices.hint: Strength and nerve. The Warden guards it.

success.text: The crown comes away in your hands. Beneath it, a relic shard of the old kings.

failure.text: The skeleton's hand closes on your wrist. The water rises — and the Warden rises with it.

choices.label: Honor the drowned king
choices.hint: Faith. Take only what is given.

success.text: The water stills. At your feet, the king's own gift.

failure.text: Your words go unheeded. You leave with nothing but the memory.

flooded_vault.name: The Flooded Vault
flooded_vault.text: Behind a door warped by centuries of water lies the city's vault — and it is still sealed.

success.text: The seal breaks. Bars of gold, and a broken relic among them.

failure.text: The door gives way all at once and the vault floods. You save what you can.

choices.label: Breach the wall beside it
choices.hint: Strength. The mire may pour in.

success.text: You break through into the vault.

failure.text: Mud and water pour through the breach.

bell_below.name: The Bell Below
bell_below.text: A great bronze bell hangs in a drowned tower, green with age. Legend says it rang to call the city's guardian.

success.text: The note rolls through the water. A hidden niche opens: an offering to whoever dared.

failure.text: Something vast answers the bell.

choices.label: Strip the bell tower
choices.hint: Strength. Bronze, and the bellmaker's offerings.

success.text: You pry away the offerings set in the tower walls.

failure.text: The bell crashes down and nearly takes you with it.

success.text: The bell's rim names the city and the roads that once led to it.

failure.text: The verdigris has eaten the words.

barrow_kings_rest.name: The Barrow-King's Rest
barrow_kings_rest.text: The heart of the barrow: a king laid out in bronze mail on a bier of stone, his grave-goods heaped about him and a broken relic upon his breast.

choices.label: Take the relic from his breast

success.text: Your fingers close on the shard. The king sleeps on.

failure.text: His eyes open. The Barrow-King rises and strides out into the world.

choices.label: Lay him to rest properly
choices.hint: Faith. Earn the dead king's blessing.

success.text: With rites he never received, the king is at peace — and his shade presses a gift into your hand.

failure.text: The rites falter. The dead do not forgive.

burial_treasury.name: The Burial Treasury
burial_treasury.text: Chests, urns and weapons heaped in a sealed chamber — a king's wealth, buried so he would not be poor in death.

choices.label: Plunder it all
choices.hint: Strength. Great riches; a curse is likely.

success.text: Gold, gems, and finery beyond counting.

failure.text: You fill your packs — and something fills them back.

success.text: You pick out the finest piece: an artifact of the old age, and a shard among the urns.

failure.text: You choose poorly — gilded lead.

hall_of_judgement.name: The Hall of Judgement
hall_of_judgement.text: Scales of black stone stand before a sealed door. Carvings show the dead weighed against a feather; the unworthy are devoured.

choices.label: Submit to the scales
choices.hint: Faith and karma. The worthy pass.

success.text: The scales balance. The door opens on the sanctum of a forgotten faith.

failure.text: The scales tip. The floor opens beneath you.

success.text: A coin's weight in the right place, and the door grinds open.

failure.text: The hall knows a cheat.

throne_of_old_king.name: Throne of the Old Kingdom
throne_of_old_king.text: A vaulted throne room deep beneath the ruins, the banners rotted to threads. Before the throne stands the last sentinel of the Old Kingdom.

choices.label: Challenge the sentinel
choices.hint: Combat. The throne's treasure lies beyond.

success.text: The sentinel falls. On the throne lies a shard of the old kings' relic.

failure.text: The sentinel drives you back, then follows you up into the light.

choices.label: Kneel as a subject
choices.hint: Charisma. Perhaps it remembers its oaths.

success.text: The sentinel lowers its blade and steps aside, as for a rightful heir.

failure.text: It does not know you. Its blade says so.

sealed_reliquary.name: The Sealed Reliquary
sealed_reliquary.text: A chapel at the root of the ruins, its reliquary sealed with seven locks. Fragments of a legend lie within.

success.text: One by one the locks give. Inside: a relic shard and the treasure it was buried with.

failure.text: The seventh lock bites. The reliquary seals itself forever.

success.text: The locks fall open of their own accord.

failure.text: Silence. The locks stay shut.

hall_of_maps.name: The Hall of Maps
hall_of_maps.text: A domed chamber painted floor to ceiling with a map of the world as the Old Kingdom knew it — roads, cities, and places no living map shows.

success.text: Your copy shows a forgotten site — and a cache the old cartographers marked with a crown.

failure.text: Your copy is crude, but something.

success.text: Behind the painted sea, a vault of instruments and a relic shard.

failure.text: A painted door, and nothing behind it.

deepest_seam.name: The Deepest Seam
deepest_seam.text: At the very bottom of the mine, the reason it was dug: a seam of gold running bright through the black rock.

choices.label: Dig out the gold
choices.hint: Strength; tools help. The roof is old.

success.text: Nuggets as big as your thumb.

failure.text: The roof groans and comes down. You scramble out with a handful.

choices.label: Survey the seam for its owners' marks

success.text: Chiselled marks name the realm that dug here, and where its other mines lay.

failure.text: Just scratches in the rock.

thing_they_woke.name: The Thing They Woke
thing_they_woke.text: The miners dug too deep. In a cavern of fused glass, a wyrm lies coiled on the gold it hoarded — and on their bones.

success.text: The wyrm dies screaming. Its hoard — and its scales — are yours.

failure.text: The wyrm's fire drives you up the shafts, and it follows you out into the world.

choices.label: Steal from the edge of the hoard

success.text: You fill your pockets and creep away.

failure.text: A coin slides. One great eye opens.

foremans_strongroom.name: The Foreman's Strongroom
foremans_strongroom.text: An iron door set into the rock: the strongroom where the mine's wages and charters were kept.

success.text: A payroll never paid, the mine's charter — and an odd shard in a velvet box.

failure.text: The lock is beyond you. You scrape a few coins from beneath the door.

success.text: The door blows in. The strongroom's contents mostly survive.

failure.text: The blast brings down the gallery.

wyrm_hoard.name: The Wyrm's Hoard
wyrm_hoard.text: The cave's last chamber reeks of sulphur. Something huge sleeps on a heap of gold and bones.

success.text: It never fully wakes. The hoard is yours.

failure.text: It wakes. You flee, and it follows the scent of its stolen gold.

success.text: Coins and a curious shard, lifted from beneath its very nose.

failure.text: Its breath scorches the cave as you run.

painted_cavern.name: The Painted Cavern
painted_cavern.text: The walls are covered with painted hunts, migrations, and the faces of the first peoples. At the cavern's end, an ancient altar.

choices.label: Study the paintings
choices.hint: Intelligence. Learn the first peoples' story.

success.text: The paintings tell where a people came from — and where they hid their sacred things.

failure.text: The story eludes you, but you sketch what you can.

choices.label: Make an offering at the altar

success.text: The old spirits accept your offering, and return one of their own.

failure.text: The spirits are silent.

underground_lake.name: The Underground Lake
underground_lake.text: A still black lake fills the cave's heart. On an islet at its centre, something gleams on a stone plinth.

choices.label: Swim to the islet
choices.hint: Strength. The water is cold and deep.

success.text: On the plinth: a relic shard in a nest of offerings.

failure.text: Something in the lake pulls you under.

success.text: You pole across dry and calm.

failure.text: The raft comes apart halfway.

underworld._comment: The Underworld — heat, the Thieves' Guild, contraband, fences and the black market. Read by src/systems/underworld.js (DataLoader.underworld).

guardStrength._holding: In the player's own holdings: + fx.raidReduction x holdingWatch (watchtower, walls) + stationed troops x holdingGarrisonPer (up to holdingGarrisonMax)

pickpocket.name: Work the Crowd
pickpocket.description: Lift purses in the market. Small pickings, small risk.

burglary.name: Burgle a Merchant's House
burglary.description: Slip into a merchant's townhouse by night. Coin and goods — the goods will be hot.

racket.name: Start a Protection Racket
racket.description: Lean on the shopkeepers. Pays every week; the watch hears about it every week too.

heist.name: Plan a Heist
heist.description: The big score. Plan it step by step, then strike.

case.name: Case the target
case.description: Watch the guards' rounds for a night.

tools.name: Buy lockpicks & rope
tools.description: Proper tools from the guild quartermaster.

crew.name: Hire a crew
crew.description: A lookout, a climber and a cracksman.

inside_man.name: Buy an inside man
inside_man.description: A servant who leaves a door unlatched.

escape.name: Plan the getaway
escape.description: Horses and a bolt-hole. Halves the chance of arrest if it goes wrong.

warnings.watched: The watch eyes you as you pass the gate.
warnings.poster: Wanted posters bearing your likeness hang by the gate.
warnings.warrant: The crown has a warrant out for you here — the guards are looking.

light.label: Light
light.blurb: The realm prospers and loves you; your purse fills slowly.

heavy.label: Heavy
heavy.blurb: The treasury and your purse swell; the realm grumbles.

peace.label: Seek peace
peace.blurb: Your marshals declare no wars and your envoys seek to end the ones you are in.

defensive.label: Defensive
defensive.blurb: Hold what you have. The court declares no wars without your word.

aggressive.label: Aggressive
aggressive.blurb: Your marshals may declare war on weak rivals as they see fit.

tolerant.label: Tolerant
tolerant.blurb: All faiths may worship freely. Trade and calm, less zeal.

devout.label: Devout
devout.blurb: The crown keeps the realm's faith, as kings always have.

zealous.label: Zealous
zealous.blurb: The crown champions the faith. Piety and loyalty rise; dissenters grow restless.

regent.label: Regency
regent.text: {kingdom} is ruled by a regent, {incumbent}. Its great lords whisper of a stronger hand.

young_heir.label: Weak heir
young_heir.text: Young {incumbent} has taken the throne of {kingdom}, and older kin think the crown sits on the wrong head.

distant_relative.label: Distant heir
distant_relative.text: With no direct heir, a distant relative, {incumbent}, claims the throne of {kingdom}. Rivals stir.

disputed.label: Disputed succession
disputed.text: The succession in {kingdom} is disputed. {incumbent} holds the palace, but not the realm.

heir.label: Rival claimant
heir.text: {incumbent} inherits {kingdom}, but a rival of the blood refuses to kneel.

holdings._comment: Holdings development (src/systems/holdings.js): projects the player builds in the settlements they rule, governors, garrisons, unrest and rebellion. Each project effect is read by an existing system: tax/happiness/growth by Taxation (marketDynamics.js), reserveDays by Economy.foodReserveDays (lean season), goods by Economy.produceDaily, salePrice by Economy.saleBonus, recruitDiscount by Economy.recruitCostMultiplier, recruitCapacity by PlayerMilitary.getRecruitmentCapacity, defense/militia by RealmWars sieges, player sieges and bandit raids, raidReduction by Holdings raids, faith by Religion.addPresence, heatRelief by Underworld.addHeat, portPrices and port repairs by Ships, settlers and growth by Colonization, petitionDays by Petitions, order by Holdings unrest.

raids._marketShare: A raid that gets in burns marketShare x foodLoss of the town market's stores, which damages the player's works there (SettlementMarket.loot)

palisade.name: Palisade
palisade.description: A ditch and a ring of sharpened stakes. Keeps out bandits and slows a war host.

stone_walls.name: Stone Walls
stone_walls.description: Replaces the palisade with curtain walls and a gatehouse.

market_square.name: Market Square
market_square.description: A paved square with stalls and a weigh-house. Traders come, and so does coin.

granary.name: Granary
granary.description: Raised stores against the lean weeks. The town counts as having more food put by.

shrine.name: Shrine
shrine.description: A wayside shrine. If you founded a faith, it is yours that is tended here.

temple.name: Temple
temple.description: Raises the shrine into a temple with its own priests.

barracks.name: Barracks
barracks.description: Quarters and a drill yard. A local militia, more and cheaper recruits, and a cheaper garrison.

harbour.name: Harbour
harbour.description: Quays and a breakwater. Only a holding beside the water can build one.

watchtower.name: Watchtower
watchtower.description: Lookouts on the roads. Bandits are seen coming, and the watch is yours.

workshop_quarter.name: Workshop Quarter
workshop_quarter.description: Streets of smiths, coopers and weavers.

tavern_inn.name: Tavern and Inn
tavern_inn.description: Ale, beds and gossip. Travellers stop, and some of them stay.

moot_hall.name: Moot Hall
moot_hall.description: Where the town meets and your court sits. Petitioners wait longer and quarrels cool.

rivals._comment: Rival adventurers (systems/rivals.js): named NPC adventurers who pursue the same goals as the player — delves, bounties, quests, tournaments, thrones — and remember how the player treated them.

greet: Another digger? The deep places don't share well, friend.
I've a map with your name nowhere on it.
Gold sleeps under every old stone. I mean to wake it.
friendly: Heard of a vault under the hills — come along and we split it fair.
You've good instincts. Rare in this trade.
hostile: Every tomb you empty is coin out of my purse.
boast: I came out of the last one with more than I went in with. And all my fingers.

greet: My blade's for hire, but not to you — not yet.
Coin first, then we talk.
Seen you swing a sword. Could be worse.
friendly: You ever need steel at your back, you know where I drink.
Ride with you any day. Pay's good, company's better.
hostile: Cross me again and we settle it with steel.
There's a ditch out there with room in it.
boast: Twelve fights, twelve purses. Want to be the thirteenth?

greet: If your face were on a poster, I'd already have you.
Every name on that board is mine. Keep that in mind.
Hunting the same quarry, are we?
friendly: Tip for you: the slow ones hide in the marsh hamlets.
You've a nose for the trail. I respect that.
hostile: Next bounty I see with your name on it, I'm taking.
Stay off my trail, or end up on someone's.
boast: Brought in three this season. Alive. Mostly.

greet: The restless dead do not rest themselves. Someone must go down.
Walk in the light, stranger.
Have you prayed today?
friendly: The heavens favour you. I have seen it.
Come with me into the tombs — two lamps burn brighter than one.
hostile: Your deeds are noted, and not only by me.
I will pray for you. Then I will stop you.
boast: I sent a barrow-king back to his grave last spring.

greet: Everything has a price. Even old ruins. Especially old ruins.
Fancy a partnership? No? Your loss.
Buy low, delve deep, sell high.
friendly: I keep a ledger of favours. Yours is in the black.
Partners split the risk and double the profit.
hostile: I've ruined better than you with a single letter.
Your credit is poor in every town I trade in.
boast: Bought a sunken hall for a song. Sold its silver for an opera.

greet: Crowns are only hats, until someone sits under them.
One day you'll bow to me. Practise now.
I have friends in every court.
friendly: When I am king, you'll want for nothing. Remember who stood by whom.
There is room at my table for you.
hostile: When I take the throne, your name goes on the first list.
You stand in the way of history.
boast: Three lords already owe me their seats.

greet: Draw, or step aside.
They say you can fight. I'd like to see it.
I collect famous names. Yours is getting there.
friendly: A worthy blade. Spar with me sometime — for the joy of it.
Of all the swords in this land, yours I'd least like to cross.
hostile: Our last bout isn't over. Not while we both breathe.
I'll find you at the next tourney. And the one after.
boast: Unhorsed the Earl's champion at the spring lists. Twice.

duelRefuse: Not you, friend. I'd rather drink with you.
I've nothing to prove to you.
duelWin: Yield! Ha — there's no shame in losing to me.
duelLose: Next time it goes the other way.
teamUpYes: Two lamps in the dark. I'm in — for a quarter of the take.
Partners, then. A fair cut and no knives in the back.
teamUpNo: With you? I'd sooner go down with a cave bear.
hireYes: Your coin, my sword. For ten days.
Done. Point me at the trouble.
hireNo: I don't fight for people I don't trust.
raceAccept: A race? Ha! See you at the bottom — if you get there.
raceWon: Fine. You had the faster horse.
raceLost: Too slow! I'll take that wager.
The place was empty by the time you heard of it.
ambush: Thought you'd seen the last of me?
No crowd to cheer you now.
slander: {rival} tells every tavern that {player} is a coward and a cheat.
{rival} swears {player} robs graves and sells the bones.

gash.name: Deep Gash
gash.description: A long cut that needs keeping clean.

cracked_ribs.name: Cracked Ribs
cracked_ribs.description: Every breath hurts. Riding hurts more.

broken_arm.name: Broken Arm
broken_arm.description: Splinted and slung. You fight one-handed.

head_wound.name: Head Wound
head_wound.description: A split scalp and a ringing skull.

arrow_leg.name: Arrow in the Leg
arrow_leg.description: The shaft is out, but the leg will not take your weight.

slashed_face.name: Slashed Face
slashed_face.description: A blade opened your cheek. People stare.

bite_wound.name: Savage Bite
bite_wound.description: Torn flesh from tooth and claw, quick to fester.

concussion.name: Concussion
concussion.description: The world swims when you stand too fast.

dark_dreams.name: Dark Dreams
dark_dreams.description: What you saw in the deep follows you into sleep.

chill.name: Chill
chill.description: Caught sleeping in the wet and cold.

heatstroke.name: Heatstroke
heatstroke.description: Too long under a burning sky.

marsh_fever.name: Marsh Fever
marsh_fever.description: Bad air and biting insects of the fens.

plague.name: Plague
plague.description: The great pestilence, caught in plague-struck lands.

scurvy.name: Scurvy
scurvy.description: Long weeks at sea without fresh food.

famine_fever.name: Famine Fever
famine_fever.description: Spread through the hungry crowds of the lean months.

wound_fever.name: Wound Fever
wound_fever.description: An untreated wound has turned bad and poisoned the blood.

upbringing._comment: Heirs, upbringing and legacy. Read lazily by systems/upbringing.js, systems/heirs.js and systems/legacy.js through DataLoader.upbringing. Focus/tutor rates are per year of childhood (relationships.json heirSettings.daysPerYear days). Seeds are points toward an earned trait (data/traits.json ids); a seed at or above config.seedThreshold is a childhood trait, and childhood traits become real earned traits at coming of age.

martial.name: Martial
martial.blurb: Arms, horses and the drill yard. Raises strength, combat and leadership; breeds bravery.

stewardship.name: Stewardship
stewardship.blurb: Ledgers, granaries and estates. Raises intelligence, commerce and leadership.

diplomacy.name: Diplomacy
diplomacy.blurb: Manners, letters and the art of the feast. Raises charisma and diplomacy.

learning.name: Learning
learning.blurb: Tutors, libraries and the stars. Raises intelligence, cartography and diplomacy; breeds scholars.

intrigue.name: Intrigue
intrigue.blurb: Whispers, ciphers and locked doors. Raises stealth and wits; breeds cunning (and lies).

piety.name: Piety
piety.blurb: Chapel, scripture and alms. Raises faith and charisma; breeds piety and mercy.

tutors.name: Hedge Tutor
tutors.blurb: A poor scholar who teaches a little of everything.

tutors.name: Master-at-Arms
tutors.blurb: A grizzled veteran of a dozen campaigns.

tutors.name: Retired Steward
tutors.blurb: Ran a duke's household for thirty years.

tutors.name: Court Envoy
tutors.blurb: Has carried treaties between three crowns.

tutors.name: Court Scholar
tutors.blurb: Corresponds with every library in the realms.

tutors.name: Whisperer
tutors.blurb: Nobody remembers hiring them. Everybody remembers what they knew.

events.title: The Bully
events.text: {child} comes home with a split lip. An older page has been tormenting {them} in the yard for weeks.

choices.label: Teach {them} to hit back
choices.result: {child} bloodies the bully's nose. Nobody tries again.

choices.label: Counsel forgiveness
choices.result: {child} offers the bully a hand. Some laugh; others remember.

choices.label: Have the bully's family punished
choices.result: The page's father loses his post. {child} learns what power is for.

events.title: A Fever
events.text: {child} burns with a fever that will not break.

choices.label: Send for a physician
choices.result: The physician's draughts do their work. {child} recovers.

choices.label: Keep vigil and pray
choices.result: The family prays through the night.

risk.result: The fever breaks, but leaves {child} frail.

choices.label: Let it run its course
choices.result: {child} sweats it out.

risk.result: The fever leaves {child} weakened for life.
risk.deathResult: The fever takes {child}. The House mourns.

events.title: A Prodigy Moment
events.text: {child} astonishes the household: {focusFeat}

choices.label: Praise {them} before the court
choices.result: {child} glows with pride.

choices.label: Push {them} harder
choices.result: {child} works twice as hard, and smiles half as often.

choices.label: Keep {them} humble
choices.result: {child} learns that talent is a duty, not a crown.

events.title: A Scandal
events.text: Servants whisper that {child} was caught in the cellars with a stable hand and a stolen cask of wine.

choices.label: Punish {them} publicly
choices.result: {child} is whipped before the household. The gossip dies; so does some of {their} warmth.

choices.label: Deny everything
choices.result: The House denies it. {child} learns that a lie told firmly is a kind of truth.

choices.label: Laugh it off
choices.result: You laugh, and the court laughs with you. {child} develops a taste for wine.

events.title: A Duel Challenge
events.text: A rival lord's son challenges {child} to a duel with blunted blades before the whole tourney field.

choices.label: Let {them} accept
choices.result: Steel rings across the field.

win.result: {child} wins! The crowd roars the House's name.

lose.result: {child} is beaten in the dust, but rises with a scar and a grudge.

choices.label: Name a champion in {their} place
choices.result: A hired sword fights for {child}. People notice.

choices.label: Decline politely
choices.result: {child} bows out with grace.

events.title: A Religious Calling
events.text: {child} says {they} dreamed of a burning light and wishes to spend the summer at a monastery.

choices.label: Let {them} go
choices.result: {child} returns quiet, certain, and changed.

choices.label: Send {them} to the fiercest preachers
choices.result: {child} returns with fire in {their} eyes and opinions about heretics.

choices.label: Forbid it: duty first
choices.result: {child} stays. The light fades, mostly.

events.title: The First Hunt
events.text: {child} rides out on {their} first hunt. A wounded boar breaks from the brush.

choices.label: Urge {them} to finish it
choices.result: {child} plants the spear.

win.result: {child} kills the boar and is blooded by the huntsmen.

lose.result: The boar's tusk opens {child}'s leg before the huntsmen kill it.

choices.label: Let the huntsmen take it
choices.result: {child} watches, and learns.

choices.label: Let {them} chase the deer into the hills
choices.result: {child} comes home two days late, scratched and delighted.

events.title: A Beggar at the Gate
events.text: {child} finds a starving family at the castle gate and asks what should be done.

choices.label: Let {them} feed them from the kitchens
choices.result: {child} serves the bread {themself}.

choices.label: Offer the father work
choices.result: {child} learns that charity can be a bargain.

choices.label: Have the guards chase them off
choices.result: {child} watches them go and says nothing.

events.title: The Locked Library
events.text: {child} has been picking the lock of the old library at night to read forbidden histories.

choices.label: Give {them} the key
choices.result: {child} disappears into the stacks for a season.

choices.label: Praise the lockpicking
choices.result: {child} grins. Locks will never stop {them} again.

choices.label: Scold {them} for sneaking
choices.result: {child} apologises and, for once, means it.

events.title: Dice in the Stables
events.text: {child} has been winning the stable boys' wages at dice. Some say the dice are loaded.

choices.label: Make {them} return the coin
choices.result: {child} hands it back, red-faced.

choices.label: Let {them} keep the winnings
choices.result: {child} keeps the coin and the habit.

choices.label: Show {them} how the cheat works
choices.result: {child} learns how a trick is done, and how to spot one.

events.title: The Children's Court
