events.text: The castle children hold a mock court, and {child} is chosen to judge a quarrel over a stolen puppy.

choices.label: Encourage a fair hearing
choices.result: {child} hears both sides and finds a compromise.

choices.label: Encourage a harsh sentence
choices.result: {child} sentences the thief to the stocks. The other children fear {them} a little.

choices.label: Suggest {they} take the puppy's biscuits as a fee
choices.result: {child} rules for whoever brings sweets.

events.title: Dreams of the Sea
events.text: {child} spends every spare hour at the docks, begging captains for stories, and asks to sail with the next ship.

choices.label: Let {them} sail a short voyage
choices.result: {child} comes back sunburnt, salt-crusted and full of charts.

choices.label: Keep {them} home
choices.result: {child} sulks for a week, then returns to {their} studies.

events.title: A Sibling Feud
events.text: {child} and {sibling} have come to blows over who will one day rule the House.

choices.label: Make them swear friendship
choices.result: The siblings embrace, if stiffly.

choices.label: Take {child}'s side
choices.result: {child} wins. {sibling} does not forget.

choices.label: Let them settle it themselves
choices.result: Only one of them walks away smiling.

events.title: A Wandering Mentor
events.text: A grey-cloaked traveller offers to teach {child} for a season in exchange for room and board.

choices.label: Take the stranger in
choices.result: The stranger teaches strange things, and leaves without a word.

risk.result: The stranger leaves with the House silver.

choices.label: Send them on their way
choices.result: The stranger shrugs and walks on.

events.title: Caught in a Lie
events.text: {child} swore that the broken vase was the cat's doing. The cat was outside all day.

choices.label: Talk about honesty
choices.result: {child} confesses, tearfully.

choices.label: Admire the nerve
choices.result: {child} learns that a good story is worth more than a vase.

choices.label: Thrash {them}
choices.result: {child} never lies to you again. To others, more carefully.

events.title: The Harvest Feast
events.text: {child} asks to host the village children at the harvest feast with {their} own purse.

choices.label: Pay for a grand feast
choices.result: The village sings {child}'s name for weeks.

choices.label: Let {them} host a modest one
choices.result: A pleasant evening. {child} learns to count the cost.

choices.label: Refuse: the House is not a tavern
choices.result: {child} hoards {their} purse instead.

focusFeats.martial: {child} disarmed the master-at-arms in a practice bout.
focusFeats.stewardship: {child} found a 200-gold error in the steward's ledgers.
focusFeats.diplomacy: {child} talked a visiting envoy out of a sulk and into a toast.
focusFeats.learning: {child} corrected the court astronomer's star chart.
focusFeats.intrigue: {child} learned the castle's secret passages, all of them.
focusFeats.piety: {child} recited the whole Book of Hours from memory.
focusFeats.none: {child} learned to read, ride and reckon in a single summer.

sagas._comment: Sagas (systems/sagas.js): world-scale storylines in chapters. A chapter's effects land when it begins, its daily effects each day it runs, and its next[] transitions are checked in order every day (first match wins). Effect keys are listed in Sagas.EFFECTS, transition conditions in Sagas.CONDITIONS, action requirements in Sagas.ACTION_REQUIRES. Tokens: {kingdom} {kingdom2} {settlement} {site} {rival} {villain} {faith} {heresy} {ruler} {house}. A chapter with `end` concludes the saga; rewards only reach the player when they took part (an action, an accepted saga quest or a saga petition ruled), unless an effect says always.

captain: Dame Ottilie of the Nine Spears

wyrm_wakes.name: The Wyrm Wakes
wyrm_wakes.summary: Something vast stirs under the peaks near {settlement}.

herds.title: The Vanished Herds
herds.text: Herdsmen who fled the high pastures beg your help: whole flocks gone in a night, and a scorched smell on the wind. They want silver to restock, or a sword to go up the mountain.

ignore.result: The herdsmen went away to find a braver lord.

choices.label: Pay to restock their flocks
choices.result: The herdsmen bless your name and drive new lambs to safer valleys.

choices.label: Swear to hunt the beast
choices.result: Word goes round the hill-steadings: a lord has sworn to climb the mountain.

choices.label: Tell them to guard their own flocks
choices.result: They leave muttering about lords who sleep behind walls.

tremors.title: Tremors
tremors.text: The earth shudders under the peaks above {settlement}. Shepherds speak of a warm wind breathing out of a cleft in the rock, and the goats will not graze near it.
tremors.rumor: Shepherds from {settlement} swear the mountain is breathing.

effects.name: Tremors
effects.text: The ground shakes in {kingdom}; miners refuse the deep shafts.

actions.label: Climb to the cleft
actions.text: You find claw-marks as long as your arm and a cave mouth that breathes like a forge.

vanishing.title: The Vanishing Herds
vanishing.text: Livestock vanish from the high pastures around {settlement} — whole flocks in a night. A herdsman swears he saw wings blot out the moon. Meat and wool grow dear.
vanishing.rumor: Flocks are vanishing around {settlement}. Something with wings is eating well.

effects.name: Vanishing Herds
effects.text: Flocks vanish from the pastures of {kingdom}.

effects.news: {rival} buys rope and lamp-oil in {settlement}, asking the way to the high cleft.

actions.label: Leave offerings of gold at the cleft
actions.text: You leave a chest of coin at the cave mouth. In the morning it is gone, and the flocks are left alone a while.

raids.title: Fire on the Roofs
raids.text: The wyrm wakes fully. It quarters the sky above {kingdom}, burning thatch and carrying off cattle, and roads empty as travellers hide. A bounty is cried in every market.
raids.rumor: The wyrm of {site} burns a village every few days. They say it lairs in the cleft above {settlement}.

effects.name: Wyrm Raids
effects.text: A wyrm burns the villages of {kingdom}.

effects.title: Slay the Wyrm of {site}
effects.text: A wyrm burns the villages of {kingdom}. Find it — it hunts from the cleft above {settlement} — and kill it.

effects.news: {rival} swears before the shrine of {settlement} to bring back the wyrm's head.

daily.text: The wyrm fell on {target} — roofs burned and folk were taken.

actions.label: Parley with the wyrm
actions.text: You stand before the wyrm with your hands empty and your purse open. It considers you with an eye like a furnace door — and names its price.

the_hunt.title: The Hunt
the_hunt.text: {rival} rides for the cleft above {settlement} with a dozen hired spears and a ballista on a mule-cart. The whole of {kingdom} waits for smoke.
the_hunt.rumor: {rival} has gone up the mountain after the wyrm. Nobody is betting on them coming down.

slain.title: Wyrmslayer
slain.text: The wyrm of {site} is dead, its bulk steaming on the hillside. {kingdom} rings its bells; the hoard in the lair still waits for someone bold enough to go in.

effects.chronicle: {house} slew the Wyrm of {site} and the bells of {kingdom} rang for three days.

effects.news: {rival} arrived at the cleft to find the wyrm already dead, and swore about it.

bargain.title: The Wyrm's Bargain
bargain.text: Gold has done what swords would not: the wyrm takes its tribute and sleeps again under the mountain. {kingdom} breathes — and wonders who will pay next year.

effects.chronicle: {house} struck a bargain with the Wyrm of {site}, and it sleeps on a bed of their gold.

lair_robbed.title: The Stolen Hoard
lair_robbed.text: Someone crept into the lair while the wyrm hunted and came out with its hoard. It returned to an empty bed, burned {settlement} in its rage, and flew east over the sea, never to return.

effects.chronicle: {house} robbed the Wyrm of {site} of its hoard. {settlement} paid for it in fire.

felled_by_others.title: The Wyrm Falls
felled_by_others.text: The wyrm is brought down — not by any hero of song, but by spears and luck. Its carcass is sold by the pound in the markets of {kingdom}.

rival_slays.title: {rival}, Wyrmslayer
rival_slays.text: {rival} comes down from the mountain with the wyrm's head on a cart and the hoard on three more. Songs are already being written. None of them mention you.

effects.news: {rival} slew the Wyrm of {site} and is hailed Wyrmslayer.

wyrm_reigns.title: The Wyrm's Shadow
wyrm_reigns.text: No one kills the wyrm. Glutted, it crawls back into the mountain to sleep — but the high valleys of {kingdom} are emptied, and a shadow lies on the land for a season.

effects.name: The Wyrm's Shadow
effects.text: {kingdom} lives in the shadow of a sleeping wyrm.

effects.news: {rival} came back from the wyrm's mountain alone, and will not speak of it.

grey_cough.name: The Grey Cough
grey_cough.summary: A dry grey cough spreads from {settlement}, and a cult says it is a judgement.

quarantine.title: Close the Gates?
quarantine.text: The grey cough is in the next valley. Your steward begs leave to close the roads and burn the bedding of the sick; the merchants beg you not to.

ignore.result: No order came. Some closed their doors, some did not.

choices.label: Close the roads and burn the bedding
choices.result: The roads are chained. Trade suffers, but the cough stops at your border.

choices.label: Keep trade flowing
choices.result: The carts keep rolling — and some of them carry the cough.

choices.label: Order prayers in every chapel
choices.result: The bells ring for the sick from dawn to dusk.

whispers.title: The Censer-Bearers
whispers.text: A dry, grey cough spreads in the lanes of {settlement}. Hooded preachers swing censers of bitter smoke and say it is the judgement of {faith} on the wicked.
whispers.rumor: There's a cough in {settlement} that turns the spit grey. The hooded ones say only the faithful will be spared.

effects.name: The Grey Cough
effects.text: A grey cough spreads in {kingdom}.

actions.label: Consult the physicians of {settlement}
actions.text: The physicians are certain of one thing: the cough came with the censer-smoke, and the censers came out of an old sealed hospice in the hills.

plague.title: Plague
plague.text: The grey cough becomes a killing plague. Carts of the dead leave {settlement} at dawn; the {heresy} preach in the squares, and the old physicians whisper of a cure sealed in a ruined hospice nearby.
plague.rumor: Plague in {kingdom}. A physician in {settlement} says the cure lies in the old sealed hospice outside town.

effects.title: A Cure for the Grey Cough
effects.text: Plague grips {kingdom}. Delve the Sealed Hospice near {settlement} for the cure the old physicians hid there — or fund a scholar to rediscover it.

actions.label: Fund a scholar to rediscover the cure
actions.text: You pay for books, a laboratory and a brave young physician. She works through the nights.

actions.label: Break the censer-bearers' processions
actions.text: Your men scatter the processions and smash the censers in the square. The smoke clears from the lanes.

the_scholar.title: The Scholar's Vigil
the_scholar.text: In a borrowed cellar in {settlement} a young physician boils roots and reads crumbling herbals by candlelight, testing each draught on the dying.
the_scholar.rumor: Your scholar in {settlement} hasn't slept in days. They say she's close.

spreads.title: The Cough Spreads
spreads.text: Nobody finds the cure. The plague leaps the border into {kingdom2}, and the two courts trade accusations as their dead are counted.
spreads.rumor: The plague has crossed into {kingdom2}. The hospice near {settlement} still stands sealed.

cured.title: The Cure
cured.text: The cure is found — a bitter draught of willow, hellebore and something stranger. Physicians carry it house to house; the carts stop running, and the {heresy} lose their congregations overnight.

effects.chronicle: {house} brought the cure for the Grey Cough to {kingdom}.

burns_out.title: The Plague Burns Out
burns_out.text: The plague burns itself out as plagues do, having taken whom it wanted. {kingdom} buries its dead; the {heresy} keep their converts.

effects.chronicle: {house} broke the censer-bearers of {settlement}, though the plague outran them.
{house} closed its roads to the Grey Cough, and its lands were spared.

lost_heir.name: The Lost Heir
lost_heir.summary: A child thought dead may sit the throne of {kingdom}.

audience.title: An Envoy of the Pretender
audience.text: A grey-cloaked envoy kneels before you with a letter sealed in purple. The one who claims the throne of a neighbouring realm asks for your friendship — and your gold.

ignore.result: The envoy left without an answer, which is an answer.

choices.label: Send gold and good wishes
choices.result: The envoy bows low. Your name will be remembered if the cause prospers.

choices.label: Refuse to meddle in another realm's quarrels
choices.result: The envoy goes away grim-faced.

choices.label: Seize the envoy and send him to the king
choices.result: The envoy is sent in chains to the court he fled. The king will be grateful.

whispers.title: A Signet Ring
whispers.text: In the taverns of {kingdom} they whisper that the old king's grandchild, thought burned with the summer palace twenty years ago, lives — and wears the royal signet on a cord around their neck.
whispers.rumor: They say a lost heir of {kingdom} lives in hiding near {settlement}.

actions.label: Seek out the claimant near {settlement}
actions.text: You find the claimant in a farmhouse: young, proud, and holding a ring that is either the true signet or a very good forgery.

gathering.title: Lords in the Night
gathering.text: Riders come and go from a farmhouse outside {settlement} by night. Lords of {kingdom} who have quarrelled with {ruler} are visiting the claimant one by one, and leaving with their minds made up.
gathering.rumor: Lords of {kingdom} are riding out to {settlement} by night to kneel to someone. The claimant is gathering a party.

actions.label: Seek out the claimant near {settlement}
actions.text: You are shown into a candle-lit room full of armed men. The claimant is young, proud, and holding a ring that is either the true signet or a very good forgery.

actions.label: Warn {ruler} of the gathering
actions.text: You send word to the court. {ruler}'s men ride out, but the farmhouse is empty when they arrive — and someone has noted your name.

pretender.title: The Pretender
pretender.text: {villain} comes forward at {settlement} bearing the royal signet and a story of fire and flight. Half the court of {ruler} kneels; the other half sharpens knives. {kingdom} is in crisis.
pretender.rumor: {villain} claims the throne of {kingdom}. You can back a claimant at court, if you have the coin.

effects.title: The Pretender's Throne
effects.text: {villain} claims the throne of {kingdom}. Back the claim, wed the claimant, or expose a fraud — but see it ended.

effects.news: {rival} rides to {settlement} to swear a sword to {villain}.

actions.label: Expose {villain} as a fraud
actions.text: Your agents find the goldsmith who cut the 'signet' and the actor who coached the story. You lay it all before the court.

actions.label: Offer your hand to {villain}
actions.text: A match is made: if {villain} is crowned, your House stands beside the throne — and holds a claim to it.

actions.label: Raise your banner for {villain}
actions.text: You ride into {settlement} beneath your banner and the pretender's side by side. Lords who were wavering come over.

crowned.title: Long Live the Heir
crowned.text: {villain} is crowned in {kingdom}, ring and story and all. Whether the blood is true no longer matters: the crown makes it so.

effects.chronicle: {house} was joined by marriage to {villain}, crowned in {kingdom}.
{house} rode beneath the banner of {villain}, and saw them crowned.

pretender_falls.title: The Pretender Falls
pretender_falls.text: The court of {kingdom} closes ranks. {villain} is taken at a river ford and the signet is hammered flat in the castle forge.

effects.chronicle: {house} was betrothed to the pretender {villain}, and shared the shame of their fall.

exposed.title: The Fraud Unmasked
exposed.text: Before the whole court of {kingdom}, the goldsmith names his customer. {villain} flees in the night; {ruler} rewards the one who saved the throne.

effects.chronicle: {house} unmasked the pretender {villain} before the court of {kingdom}.

long_winter.name: The Long Winter
long_winter.summary: The frost came early to {kingdom}, and the granaries are emptying.

bread.title: Bread or the Gallows
bread.text: The bakers' guild has been caught selling bread cut with sawdust while the corn-chandlers hoard grain. The hungry crowd outside your hall wants someone hanged; the guild wants your protection.

ignore.result: With no ruling, the crowd broke the bakers' windows itself.

choices.label: Open your own stores to the hungry
choices.result: Loaves go out from your kitchens. The crowd goes home fed and quiet.

choices.label: Hang the worst of the hoarders
choices.result: A corn-chandler swings in the square. Strangely, grain appears in the market next morning.

choices.label: Protect the guild — for a fee
choices.result: The guild pays handsomely. The crowd remembers.

early_frost.title: Early Frost
early_frost.text: The frost comes early to {kingdom}, blackening the late harvest in the fields. The elders read hard signs in the geese flying south a month too soon.
early_frost.rumor: The frost took half the late harvest in {kingdom}. Grain merchants are already smiling.

effects.name: Early Frost
effects.text: An early frost blackens the fields of {kingdom}.

hunger.title: The Hungry Months
hunger.text: Winter will not end. The granaries of {kingdom} empty while corn-chandlers in {settlement} sit on locked barns, waiting for prices to climb higher. The thieves' guild is buying in.
hunger.rumor: Bread costs a day's wage in {settlement}. Everyone knows whose barns are full — and that the guild has a share.

effects.name: Hoarded Granaries
effects.text: Grain hoarders hold {kingdom} to ransom.

effects.title: Bread for {settlement}
effects.text: {settlement} is starving while hoarders sit on full barns. Bring food, or break the barns open.

actions.label: Give 40 food to the poor of {settlement}
actions.text: You hand out food from carts in the square until there is none left. Nobody in {settlement} will forget it.

actions.label: Break open the hoarders' barns
actions.text: Your men smash the locks and the grain pours out into the street. The guild will want a word with you.

actions.label: Buy into the hoarders' ring
actions.text: You put up silver for a share of the locked barns. When the price peaks, you will be paid.

bread_riots.title: Bread Riots
bread_riots.text: The hungry storm the corn exchange of {settlement}. The watch fires into the crowd; barns burn with the grain still in them.
bread_riots.rumor: There were riots in {settlement}. They burned the barns rather than let them stay locked.

effects.name: Bread Riots
effects.text: Bread riots shake {kingdom}.

thaw_relieved.title: The Thaw
thaw_relieved.text: The thaw comes at last, and {settlement} lives to see it. The hoarders' prices collapse; their barns are opened by order of {ruler}, who is glad to have someone else to thank.

effects.chronicle: {house} fed {settlement} through the Long Winter.

thaw_profiteer.title: A Fat Spring
thaw_profiteer.text: Spring comes, the hoarders sell at the top of the market, and a share of the take comes to you. {kingdom} remembers the winter — and who grew rich on it.

effects.chronicle: {house} grew rich on the hunger of {kingdom} in the Long Winter.

thaw_bitter.title: A Bitter Spring
thaw_bitter.text: The thaw comes too late for many. {kingdom} counts its graves, and the songs of the Long Winter are all about the hoarders.

sea_reavers.name: Sea Reavers
sea_reavers.summary: {villain} gathers a reaver fleet off the coast of {kingdom}.

coast.title: Fire Along the Coast
coast.text: Fisherfolk whose village was burned by reavers crowd your hall. They want boats rebuilt, men to stand watch on the cliffs, or leave to arm themselves.

ignore.result: The fisherfolk went back to the ashes of their village.

choices.label: Pay to rebuild their boats
choices.result: New hulls go down the slipways within the month.

choices.label: Let them arm and drill as a coast watch
choices.result: Beacon fires go up on the headlands, tended by men with spears.

choices.label: The sea is the king's concern, not yours
choices.result: They go away to find a lord who owns a ship.

black_sails.title: Black Sails
black_sails.text: Black sails off {settlement}. A reaver called {villain} has burned two fishing villages and is sending word to every cutthroat captain on the sea: come and get rich.
black_sails.rumor: {villain} is gathering captains off {settlement}. Fishermen won't put out past the headland.

effects.name: Black Sails
effects.text: Reavers prowl the coast of {kingdom}.

fleet.title: The Reaver Fleet
fleet.text: {villain} has a fleet now — a dozen hulls and a flagship with a gilded figurehead. Coastal towns of {kingdom} are raided by night; the price of everything that comes by sea climbs.
fleet.rumor: {villain}'s flagship has been seen off {settlement}. Sink it and the fleet scatters, they say.

effects.name: Reaver Fleet
effects.text: A reaver fleet blockades the coast of {kingdom}.

effects.title: Sink {villain}'s Flagship
effects.text: The reaver {villain} raids the coast of {kingdom}. Sink the flagship and the fleet will scatter.

daily.text: Reavers came ashore at {target} by night.

actions.label: Pay {villain} to raid elsewhere
actions.text: A purse of gold goes out to the flagship in a rowing boat. {villain}'s answer comes back: a bow, and a promise to sail for richer coasts.

actions.label: Fund the royal fleet of {kingdom}
actions.text: Your gold buys pitch, timber and crews for the royal fleet. Its admiral salutes you.

sea_battle.title: The Battle of the Headland
sea_battle.text: The royal fleet of {kingdom} sails out to meet {villain} off {settlement}. For two days the smoke of burning ships hangs over the water.
sea_battle.rumor: The king's ships have gone out against {villain}. Every widow in {settlement} is on the cliffs.

reavers_broken.title: The Flagship Burns
reavers_broken.text: {villain}'s flagship goes down in flames, and the reaver fleet scatters like crows from a gunshot. Bells ring in every harbour of {kingdom}.

effects.chronicle: {house} sank the flagship of the reaver {villain} off {settlement}.

reavers_bought.title: Paid to Go
reavers_bought.text: {villain} takes the gold and sails away — to raid some other coast with ships your silver repaired. The harbours of {kingdom} reopen; elsewhere, others pay.

effects.name: Emboldened Reavers
effects.text: Paid-off reavers roam the seas.

effects.chronicle: {house} paid the reaver {villain} to leave the coast of {kingdom}.

crown_victory.title: The Crown's Victory
crown_victory.text: The royal fleet of {kingdom} breaks the reavers. {villain} is hanged from the yardarm of their own flagship, and the admiral is the hero of the hour.

effects.chronicle: {house} paid for the ships that broke the reaver {villain}.

reaver_coast.title: The Reaver Coast
reaver_coast.text: The royal fleet is beaten. {villain} styles themself Lord of the Reaver Coast, and every ship that passes {settlement} pays toll or burns.

effects.name: The Reaver Coast
effects.text: {villain} rules the sea-lanes off {kingdom}.

effects.chronicle: The beacon-watch {house} raised kept the reavers of {villain} from its own shores.

sundering_faith.name: The Sundering Faith
sundering_faith.summary: A barefoot preacher is splitting the faith of {kingdom} in two.

council.title: Which Altar?
council.text: Two delegations wait in your hall: the bishop's clerks with a writ against the new preaching, and a crowd of the preacher's followers with a petition of their own. Each wants your name on their side.

ignore.result: You signed nothing. Both sides took it as an insult.

choices.label: Sign the bishops' writ
choices.result: The preacher's followers are turned out of your chapels.

choices.label: Sign the reformers' petition
choices.result: The reformers cheer your name in the streets. The bishop does not.

choices.label: Sign neither, and call for a council
choices.result: You pay for a hall and a feast. Both sides come, if only to argue.

preacher.title: The Barefoot Preacher
preacher.text: {villain} walks barefoot into {settlement} and preaches against the gold of the {faith} bishops. Thousands come to hear; the bishops call it the {heresy}.
preacher.rumor: There's a preacher called {villain} in {settlement} telling folk the bishops have sold {faith} for gold.

actions.label: Hear {villain} preach
actions.text: You stand in the crowd. {villain} speaks plainly and well — and much of it is true.

schism.title: Schism
schism.text: The council of {kingdom} splits. Half the lords take {villain}'s side; the bishops excommunicate them all. In {kingdom2}, the faithful of {faith} watch and choose sides.
schism.rumor: {kingdom} is split over {villain}. A council could heal it — if anyone had the standing to call one.

effects.name: Schism
effects.text: Schism tears at the faith of {kingdom}.

effects.title: Heal the Schism
effects.text: The faith of {kingdom} is splitting over {villain}. Call a council of reconciliation, or see one side win.

actions.label: Champion {villain}'s reforms
actions.text: You declare for the reformers. {villain} embraces you before the crowd.

actions.label: Stand with the bishops
actions.text: You kneel to the bishops and swear to defend the old order. Your men are at their disposal.

actions.label: Call a council of reconciliation
actions.text: You pay for the great hall, the feast and the guards, and you sit at the head of the table while bishops and reformers shout at each other for nine days. On the tenth, they agree.

strife.title: Holy Strife
strife.text: Mobs of reformers and loyalists fight in the streets of {settlement}. Churches burn; {kingdom2} sends priests and silver to the bishops, and relations between the realms sour.
strife.rumor: They're burning churches in {settlement}. {kingdom2} is backing the bishops.

effects.name: Holy Strife
effects.text: Holy strife burns in {kingdom}.

actions.label: Force a truce between the factions
actions.text: With your soldiers between the mobs and your gold in the bishops' coffers, a truce is sworn on the cathedral steps.

reconciled.title: The Council of Reconciliation
reconciled.text: Bishops and reformers kneel side by side. The worst of the bishops' gold goes to the poor; {villain} is made an abbot and told to stop walking barefoot. {kingdom} is whole again.

effects.chronicle: {house} healed the schism of {kingdom} at the Council of Reconciliation.

reformed.title: The Reformation
reformed.text: The reformers win. The bishops' palaces are sold, {villain} is hailed a saint in their own lifetime, and the faith of {kingdom} is plainer, poorer, and fiercer.

effects.chronicle: {house} stood with {villain} and the reformers of {kingdom}, and won.

orthodoxy.title: The Bonfire
orthodoxy.text: The bishops win. {villain} is burned in the square at {settlement} and the {heresy} is driven underground, where it will smoulder for a generation.

effects.chronicle: {house} stood with the bishops of {kingdom} when {villain} was burned.

iron_company.name: The Iron Company
iron_company.summary: The unpaid sellswords of {kingdom} are turning on their masters.

tolls.title: Tolls on the King's Road
tolls.text: Merchants complain that sellswords of the Iron Company have set up a toll-chain on the road to your gates and take a tenth of every cart. They want an escort, or a lord with the stomach to clear the road.

ignore.result: The merchants paid the toll, and charged you for it in their prices.

choices.label: Hire escorts for the merchant carts
choices.result: Carts move under your guards' spears. The sellswords watch, and let them pass.

choices.label: Pay the Company to lift the chain
choices.result: The chain comes down. For now.

choices.label: Raise a levy to clear the road
choices.result: Your levy marches out with pitchforks and old spears. The toll-chain is gone by evening.

unpaid.title: Wages in Arrears
unpaid.text: The Iron Company — three hundred sellswords in the pay of {kingdom} — have not been paid since the spring. Their captain, {villain}, has begun to speak of 'taking wages in kind'.
unpaid.rumor: The Iron Company's men are drinking on credit in {settlement}. {villain} says the crown owes them, and they'll collect.

actions.label: Pay the Company's arrears yourself
actions.text: You count out the Company's back-pay on a drumhead. {villain} bites a coin, grins, and swears the Company to your name.

rogue.title: The Company Goes Rogue
rogue.text: The Iron Company tears up its contract. {villain} leads three hundred veterans out of {settlement}, chaining roads, burning the farms of anyone who will not pay, and daring the crown of {kingdom} to stop them.
rogue.rumor: The Iron Company has turned bandit around {settlement}. {villain} will take a new contract — at a price.

effects.name: The Free Company
effects.text: The Iron Company plunders {kingdom}.

effects.title: Break the Iron Company
effects.text: The rogue Iron Company plunders {kingdom}. Beat them in the field, or buy their swords.

effects.news: {rival} has been seen drinking with {villain}'s officers.

actions.label: Buy the Company's contract
actions.text: You meet {villain} in a burned farmhouse. The price is steep, but three hundred veterans will march under your banner — for a while.

sack.title: The Sack of {settlement}
sack.text: The Iron Company storms {settlement}. For three days they loot it street by street; the crown of {kingdom} pays a ransom to make them leave.
sack.rumor: {settlement} has been sacked by the Iron Company. They're heading for the border with {kingdom2}.

broken.title: The Company Broken
broken.text: The Iron Company is broken in the field. {villain} dies with a sword in hand; the survivors scatter or sign on with honest masters. The roads of {kingdom} open again.

effects.chronicle: {house} broke the Iron Company and slew its captain, {villain}.

company_hired.title: A New Paymaster
company_hired.text: The Iron Company has a new paymaster, and it is you. {villain} keeps the Company in good order; {kingdom} breathes again and wonders what you mean to do with three hundred swords.

effects.chronicle: {house} bought the swords of the Iron Company and its captain, {villain}.

broken_by_crown.title: The King's Justice
broken_by_crown.text: The Iron Company is cut down by the crown's soldiers. {villain}'s head goes up over the gate of {settlement}.

moves_on.title: Over the Border
moves_on.text: Rich with plunder, the Iron Company crosses into {kingdom2}. Each court blames the other for letting them pass.

effects.name: The Free Company
effects.text: The Iron Company plunders {kingdom2}.

the_comet.name: The Comet
the_comet.summary: A comet with a forked tail hangs over the world, and a seer reads doom in it.

omen.title: The Forked Star
omen.text: A comet with a forked tail hangs in the night sky, brighter every evening. Astrologers argue; farmers bury coins at the crossroads for luck.
omen.rumor: Have you seen the star with two tails? The priests of {faith} say it is a warning.

effects.name: The Forked Star
effects.text: A forked comet hangs in the sky.

actions.label: Pay an astrologer to chart the comet
actions.text: Your astrologer works out the comet's path with brass and patience. It will pass, she says — and a piece of it may already have fallen, near {settlement}.

prophecy.title: The Prophecy
prophecy.text: {villain}, a seer of {settlement}, prophesies that when the comet turns red the line of {ruler} will end. A cult gathers to wait for the day; they call themselves the {heresy}.
prophecy.rumor: {villain} says the comet will turn red and {ruler}'s line will end. They say a piece of the star fell near {settlement}.

effects.name: Star Cult
effects.text: A star cult waits for doom in {kingdom}.

effects.title: The Riddle of the Comet
effects.text: {villain} prophesies doom for {kingdom}. Find what fell from the sky near {settlement}, or prove the seer wrong.
effects.objective: Solve the riddle of the comet

actions.label: Debate {villain} before the cult
actions.text: You lay your astrologer's charts before the crowd: the comet's colour is the dust of its tail, and it will pass in a month. {villain} has no answer.

reddening.title: The Red Star
reddening.text: The comet turns red as blood. Panic in {kingdom}: the cult dances in the streets of {settlement}, merchants hoard, and {ruler} doubles the guard.
reddening.rumor: The comet's gone red. The cult of {villain} says the end is days away.

effects.name: The Red Star
effects.text: Panic grips {kingdom} under a red star.

actions.label: Debate {villain} before the cult
actions.text: Even under a red sky, your charts carry the day. The comet is already fading.

starfall.title: The Star-Iron
starfall.text: In the crater lies a lump of black star-iron, warm to the touch. Displayed in {settlement}, it shows the comet for what it is: a stone from the sky. The cult of {villain} melts away.

effects.chronicle: {house} found the star-iron that fell with the Forked Comet.

debunked.title: The Seer Confounded
debunked.text: {villain} is laughed out of {settlement}. The comet fades from the sky on the night you predicted, and astrologers across {kingdom} quote your charts.

effects.chronicle: {house} confounded the seer {villain} and charted the Forked Comet.

cult_rises.title: The Cult of the Red Star
cult_rises.text: The comet fades, but the cult does not. {villain}'s followers say the doom was only delayed, and their numbers grow in {kingdom}.

fades.title: The Star Fades
fades.text: The comet fades. Nothing falls, no line ends. {villain} quietly leaves {settlement}, and in a year no one admits to having believed.

discovery._comment: Uncharted lands (src/systems/discovery.js): remote islands, hidden coves, lost valleys and sunken reefs chosen lazily from the generated map by a hash of the world seed; how they are found, named, sold, settled and contested; the exotic goods found there (merged into playerEconomy GOODS at load, never stocked by any market).

goods.name: Ambergris
goods.description: Grey treasure of the whale roads, worth its weight in silver to perfumers.

goods.name: Pearls
goods.description: Lustrous pearls from untouched oyster beds.

goods.name: Sea Silk
goods.description: Golden thread spun from the beards of giant shellfish.

goods.name: Cloudpepper
goods.description: A fiery spice that grows nowhere on any known shore.

goods.name: Blue Coral
goods.description: Coral the colour of deep water, prized by jewellers.

goods.name: Ghost Orchid
goods.description: A pale orchid from hidden valleys; physicians and princes pay dearly.

goods.name: Golden Amber
goods.description: Amber holding the insects of a vanished age.

A drunk sailor in {town} talks of a {kind} somewhere to the {dir}, about {leagues} leagues off.
An old trapper in {town} claims there is a {kind} beyond the wild country to the {dir}.
Driftwood carved by unknown hands washes up near {town}. It comes from the {dir}.

famine_relief.title: Bread for {town}
famine_relief.text: {issuer} pays well for food delivered to {town}, where the granaries run low.

siege_relief.title: Relieve {town}
siege_relief.text: {issuer} will pay a war premium for supplies run into {town} while the enemy is at the walls.

fleet_timber.title: Timber for the Fleet
fleet_timber.text: The royal shipwrights of {issuer} need {good} at {town} to build and refit the fleet.

war_iron.title: Iron for the War
war_iron.text: {issuer}'s armouries at {town} want {good} for the war.

walls_stone.title: Stone for the Walls
walls_stone.text: The masons of {town} are raising new walls for {issuer} and need {good}.

court_luxuries.title: A Court Wedding
court_luxuries.text: {issuer}'s court celebrates at {town} and orders {good} for the feast.

ventures.name: Spice Fleet to the Far Isles
ventures.text: {kingdom} fits out a fleet for the spice islands and sells shares in the cargo.

ventures.name: The Northern Whaling Voyage
ventures.text: {kingdom}'s whalers sail north and want investors for the oil.

ventures.name: The Crown Silver Mine
ventures.text: {kingdom} opens a deep silver working and offers shares in the first seams.

ventures.name: The Long Caravan East
ventures.text: {kingdom} sends a great caravan over the eastern passes and sells shares in what it brings back.

kingship._comment: Kingship — ruling a realm as its sovereign (src/systems/kingship.js, built on systems/throne.js). The royal council's great offices, realm-wide edicts with upkeep, the realm's lords as vassals (opinion, ambition, power, factions, levy refusal and revolt), and the AI's regard for a player-ruled realm. Office and edict 'mods' are kingdom bonus keys (world/kingdomState.js KingdomBonuses) fed through kingdom.crown.mods; office mods are per point of competence (1-20), scaled by the councillor's loyalty.

revolt._holdingSacked: A rebel host that storms one of the player's own holdings sacks it (unrest, garrison and people lost); it never becomes a rebel seat.

chancellor.label: Chancellor
chancellor.blurb: Foreign affairs: warmer envoys, better odds of peace, and one more edict the court can manage at 12+ competence.

marshal.label: Marshal
marshal.blurb: The royal host: armies rebuild faster and the realm keeps a larger one.

steward.label: Steward
steward.blurb: The royal treasury: more income for the crown. A disloyal steward skims.

spymaster.label: Spymaster
spymaster.blurb: Plots revealed: vassal factions come to light before they strike, and rebellion is rooted out.

highPriest.label: High Priest
highPriest.blurb: Faith unity: the realm's church draws together (and steadies the realm).

conscription.label: Conscription
conscription.blurb: Every village sends its sons. A larger, faster-mustering host; the commons and the lords' fields suffer.

road_programme.label: Road-building programme
road_programme.blurb: Royal surveyors and corvée gangs pave the king's highways. Trade and building quicken, and roads and bridges you build in the realm cost 40% less.

tolerance.label: Religious tolerance
tolerance.blurb: Every people may keep its rites. Minorities settle; the bishops fume and the church frays a little.

persecution.label: Persecution of heretics
persecution.blurb: Inquisitors ride. The faith hardens and unites; minorities seethe.

merchant_charters.label: Merchant charters
merchant_charters.blurb: Free towns and guild charters. Trade booms; the crown's dues are lighter, and a company charter from the realm costs half.

famine_dole.label: Famine dole
famine_dole.blurb: Royal granaries open to the hungry. In the lean weeks and in famine the crown ships grain to every town short of stores — paid from the treasury by the cartload — easing hunger, unrest and the famine's toll on the people. In good times it costs little.

crown_monopolies.label: Crown monopolies
crown_monopolies.blurb: Salt, iron and wine — and the tools, weapons and liquor made from them — are the crown's alone. Every town of the realm sells them only through the crown's factors, 30% dearer, and the markup goes to the royal treasury; no trading company may deal in them there. Merchants and greedy lords resent it, and rival merchant houses earn less from their posts in the realm.

royal_assizes.label: Royal assizes
royal_assizes.blurb: The king's judges ride circuit and overrule the lords' own courts. Order and loyalty — and baronial grumbling.

scutage.label: Scutage
scutage.blurb: The lords pay gold instead of knight-service. A richer crown, a smaller host, and lords who keep their men at home.

patronage.label: Royal patronage of the arts
patronage.blurb: Poets, painters and scholars at court. Learning and renown spread; foreign courts admire you.

fortification.label: Fortification of the marches
fortification.blurb: Stone castles on every border. The realm is harder to take, and your own holdings in it hold out behind stronger walls.

counsel._comment: The Steward's Counsel (src/systems/counsel.js): the advisor's rules. Each rule names a reader (Counsel.READERS) that returns facts; the fact fields fill the {placeholders} in 'text'. group: threat | opportunity | goal. severity: critical | warning | notice | info (a fact may override it). priority orders items of equal severity (a fact may add a 'boost'). panel: the ActionMenu panel the item's button opens (ui/actionMenu/counsel.js COUNSEL_PANELS); items with a map hex also get a 'show on map' button. params: per-rule tunables passed to the reader. max: items kept per rule (config.maxPerRule otherwise). heavy: whole-world scans, read at most once a day. enabled:false switches a rule off.

chatter._comment: A living world: what townsfolk say about what is happening (systems/chatter.js), the heralds' proclamations (systems/heralds.js) and the tavern's regional news (player/tavern/intel.js). Line groups are chosen by conditions on world and player state; see the manual, 'Townsfolk Talk & Heralds'.

underwriter_failed: Hear ye! {uw} of {place} cannot meet its claims and has shut its doors. Its policies are void.
{uw} is broken: too many ships lost, too many claims. Merchants of {place}, look to your cover.
great_claim: {uw} pays {amount} gold on a single claim. The underwriters of {place} grumble over their ledgers.
A great loss is made good: {uw} of {place} pays out {amount} gold.
insured_catastrophe: A great storm has sunk a fleet insured at {place}. {uw} must pay {amount} gold.
Ill news for {uw}: a whole fleet lost, and {amount} gold of claims to meet.
bourse_mania: All {place} buys {listing}! Its shares double while you sleep, they say.
A fever for {listing} grips the Bourse of {place}. Cobblers sell their lasts to buy a share.
bourse_crash: Hear ye! {listing} has crashed at the Bourse of {place}. Fortunes made in a season are gone in a morning.
The bubble is burst: {listing} falls by half at {place}, and {bank} counts its losses.
bourse_panic: Panic at the Bourse of {place}! Every share falls as the news of {bank} spreads.
The floor at {place} is in uproar: sellers and no buyers.
mine_strike: Hear ye! A new {site} is struck in the hills near {place}. Miners and carters, there is work to be had!
Strike! The prospectors of {place} have found a {site}; {good} will come down from the hills before the season is out.
By leave of the crown of {kingdom}, a {site} is opened near {place}. Let honest men go dig.
mine_vein: The old {site} near {place} has found a fresh vein: the pits will not close this year.
Good news from {place}: a new seam in the {site}, and {good} enough for years yet.
mine_exhausted: Hear ye! The {site} near {place} is worked out and its pits are shut. {good} will be dear hereabouts.
The last cart of {good} has come down from the {site} near {place}. Its miners take the road to {to}.
No more {good} from the hills of {place}: the {site} is dug out, and the price has gone up already.
mine_accident: Woe at {place}! A gallery has fallen in at the {site}: {n} miners are dead.
A fall at the {site} near {place} has killed {n}. The town blames the masters, who drive the men too hard.
guild_strike: Hear ye! The {guild} has downed tools over {reason}. There will be little {good} in {place} for {days} days.
The masters of the {guild} have shut their shops: {reason}, they say. Whoever brings {good} to {place} will sell it dear.
Strike at {place}! {master} and the {guild} will not work until the crown of {kingdom} hears them.
guild_election: The masters of the {guild} have chosen {master} to lead them.
Hear ye! {master} is guildmaster of the {guild} at {place}.
guild_chartered: By royal charter, the {guild} alone may set the trade of {place}. {master} gives thanks to the crown of {kingdom}.
Hear ye! The crown of {kingdom} grants the {guild} its charter, and its masters their privileges.
guild_abolished: Hear ye! The {guild} is broken by order of the crown. Any man may now work its trade in {place}.
The guildhall at {place} is shut and its charter burned: the {guild} is no more.
trade_embargo: Hear ye! By order of the crown of {kingdom}, no goods of {other} may be bought or sold in its markets.
The crown of {kingdom} closes its roads and harbours to the merchants of {other}. Smugglers rejoice.
Embargo! {kingdom} will have no trade with {other} until the crown says otherwise.
trade_treaty: Hear ye! {kingdom} and {other} sign a treaty of trade: no duties between them, and safe roads for their merchants.
The seals are set: the merchants of {kingdom} and {other} may cross each other's borders without paying a copper.
A treaty of commerce between {kingdom} and {other}! The carters cheer and the toll-keepers sulk.
trade_war: Hear ye! {kingdom} raises its duties on the goods of {other}, in answer to {other}'s own.
Duty upon duty: {kingdom} and {other} are at war over tariffs, and the merchants pay for both.
The customs men of {kingdom} have new orders: every cart from {other} pays dearer at the border.
trade_ban: Hear ye! While the realm goes hungry, no {good} may leave {kingdom}, by order of the crown.
The crown of {kingdom} bans the sale of {good} across its borders. Let our own be fed first!
No {good} out of {kingdom}: the border posts are turning the wagons back.
trade_granary: Hear ye! The royal granaries of {kingdom} are opened: {n} measures of grain for the hungry towns.
The crown of {kingdom} feeds its people from the royal stores. Bless the good years that filled them!
Grain carts from the royal granaries roll into the hungry towns of {kingdom}. No one starves this season.
econ_dear: Hear ye! Bread is dear in {kingdom}: food costs {pct}% more than in {since}. The crown's criers bid the carters make haste.
The criers of {kingdom} cry the price of bread: up {pct}% since {since}, and the poor feel it first.
Dear bread in {kingdom}! Food fetches {food}% of its worth, {pct}% more than in {since}. Grain bought cheap elsewhere will sell well there.
econ_inflation: Hear ye! Prices in {kingdom} have climbed {pct}% since {since}. The goodwives blame the bakers, the bakers blame the coin.
The criers of {kingdom} confess it: everything costs {pct}% more than it did in {since}.
Prices rise in {kingdom}: {pct}% since {since}. A purse of silver buys less each week.
harvest_failing: Hear ye! The harvest in {place} is failing: the fields promise barely {pct}% of a common year. Lay in grain while it is cheap.
Ill news from {place}: the crop withers in the fields, {pct}% of a fair harvest at best. Bread will be dear there by spring.
The reeves of {place} send word: a thin harvest is coming, {pct}% of the usual. The granaries will be wanted.
harvest_bumper: Hear ye! The fields of {place} stand heavy: a bumper harvest is coming, {pct}% of a common year. Grain will be cheap there.
Good news from {place}: the finest crop in memory ripens, {pct}% of the usual. The brewers rejoice.
harvest_blight: Hear ye! {blight} is in the fields of {place}. The farmers burn what they cannot save.
Woe to {place}: {blight} has come, out of {from}. Pray it stops at the river.
The criers of {place} bid all to watch their fields and herds: {blight} is abroad.
harvest_poor: Hear ye! The harvest of {place} is in, and it is poor: {pct}% of a common year. Hard months lie ahead.
The last sheaves are in at {place}: a lean harvest, {pct}% of the usual. The bakers have raised their prices already.
harvest_plenty: Hear ye! A rich harvest is gathered in {place}: {pct}% of a common year. The barns overflow and grain goes cheap.
Plenty in {place}! The harvest came in at {pct}% of the usual; the brewers and the poor alike give thanks.
fashion: Hear ye! At the court of {place}, {text}: {goods} fetch a premium wherever the fashion reaches.
News from {place}: {text}. Whoever has {goods} to sell should make for the courts.
The criers bring word from {place}: {text}, and the merchants scramble for {goods}.
labour_refugees: Hear ye! {n} souls have fled {place} for fear of {why}, and crowd the roads to {to}. Charity, good people!
The roads out of {place} are thick with carts and bundles: {n} have fled the {why} for {to} and the towns beyond.
By order of the crown of {kingdom}: let {to} open its gates to the folk of {place}, who flee the {why}.
labour_strike: Hear ye! The artisans of {place} have downed their tools: their wages buy no bread. The workshops stand cold for {days} days.
The guilds of {place} are out in the square, not at the bench: bread is dear and the masters pay the old rate.
No hammer rings in {place}: its craftsmen strike against the price of bread.
labour_boom: Hear ye! {place} prospers: work for every hand and bread on every table, and newcomers arrive by the cartload.
Times are good in {place}: the workshops hire, the stalls are full and folk are flocking in from the villages.
{place} is the place to be, say the carters: good wages, full larders and a roof for all who come.
market_fair: Hear ye! The {fair} is open in {place} for {days} days. Merchants from far lands, and every stall dealing close!
Come one, come all to the {fair} at {place}: spices, wine and wares from beyond the sea, and the stalls buying dear.
By leave of the crown of {kingdom}, the {fair} is cried at {place}. Bring your goods and your purse!
market_dearth: Hear ye! {place} goes hungry: {good} fetches {pct}% over its worth. Whoever brings food will be paid well and blessed.
The criers of {kingdom} beg for {good}: {place} is in dearth and the poor queue at the bakers' doors.
Dearth in {place}! The granaries are low and {good} is dear. Let the carters make haste.
