markets._doc: Settlement goods economy (world/settlementMarket.js, ticked daily by systems/marketDynamics.js). Every settlement keeps one inventory (settlement.market.stock) of the goods below. Production comes from the land around it, map resources (Economy.calculateDetailedProduction), player properties nearby and holdings; the people eat, burn and wear goods out every day; towns with the industry mill, bake, brew and smith. Prices for buying, selling, caravans, ports, factors and tavern talk all read the same stock: price = base x scarcity x season x weather x events (x size, local-resource discount and monopoly markup when the market sells). Scarcity = (stock / (daily need x days)) ^ -elasticity, clamped to [min, max]. NPC trade moves goods along kingdom trade routes and between near neighbours, from glut to dearth; the settlements keep the margin as their trade income.
markets._tickDays: Market day: each market (and each trade link) takes its turn every tickDays days, staggered by place, and works that many days at once â€” the same economy at a fraction of the cost per day.

price._noNeedMax: Most a town that doesn't use a good pays over base for it (it only buys to resell)

markets._goods: perCapita: units one person uses a day (x typeDemand). minType: smallest settlement that uses it. days: stock a market aims to hold, in days of need (the scarcity reference); minStock: the least it aims to hold even in a hamlet. spoil: share of stock lost a day. cap: most stock held, in multiples of the target. coldMult: use in cold weather. group: food / drink / fuel / tools / clothes / luxury (shortage effects). noNeedRef: reference need (per capita) where nobody uses the good, so a glut is still cheap.
markets._terrain: Terrain classes of the seven hexes a settlement stands on and beside: their shares drive what the land yields.
markets._fertility: Grain the land yields per terrain (1 = good farmland); the average over the seven hexes (water skipped) scales food output, clamped to [min, max].
markets._food: Food the land and waters bring in a day = the town's food need x selfSupply[type] x fertility x the food multiplier of its map resources and peoples (Economy.calculateDetailedProduction), x the season (Seasons.settlementFoodMultiplier), droughts (farmProduction) and tool shortages. It splits into grain, fish and meat: fish by water around the town and fish banks, meat by pasture and herds.

food._grainFor: Grain the brewers and distillers need per unit of their drink, added to the food the land must grow
food._seasonality: Share of the agricultural year's swing (Seasons.settlementFoodMultiplier) the market feels; granaries and cellars smooth the rest

markets._supply: Other goods the land and craftsmen supply, as a share of the town's own need: base + share of each terrain class x weight. itemGoods: what each item of Economy.calculateDetailedProduction's breakdown (map resources, after the goods bonus and the peoples' crafts) brings to market, x resourceScale units per breakdown unit; the urban 'textiles' base counts at craftScale.
markets._supplyGems2026_10: Gems 0.95 (was 0.8) and luxuries 0.7 (was 0.9): the craftsmen made most of a town's luxuries outright, so the stalls stood glutted with them (scarcity about 0.65) while gems ran short, and the jewellers (town trade and the player's works) had neither spare gems nor room to sell. Now more of the luxuries come from cutting gems (docs/economy-balance.md, Economic Chronicle).
markets._supplyHinterland2026_10: Textiles 0 (was 0.65), tools 0.7 (was 1.0): the abstract craftsmen no longer make the cloth and a third of the tools from nothing. The weavers and smiths make them from the wool, iron and coal the hinterland's sheep runs, mines and coal pits bring in (data/hinterland.json), so towns without them buy cloth and tools from towns that have them (docs/economy-balance.md, The Hinterland).
markets._saltResource: Map resources that add goods not in the breakdown: each nearby deposit adds `perDeposit` x popMod units a day (half when not on the town's own hex).
markets._recipes: Local industry, run when the output is below its target and the inputs are in store: per 1000 people a day at most `cap` runs, each turning `in` into `out` (units). minType: smallest settlement with the trade. fill: the trade works ahead of need while its inputs are in glut, up to fill x the output's target when the inputs stand at twice theirs (brewers brew the harvest's cheap grain: the after-harvest beer that lifts the mood).
markets._shortages: Shortage gauges are moving averages (alpha) of the share of the day's need left unmet. food: past `dearth` the town is in dearth (Kingship.hunger, tavern talk, chatter) and its people eat harder into the granary (Economy.produceDaily consumption +food x foodStrain). tools: production of goods and gold falls by tools x toolPenalty. fuel: in cold weather happiness falls by up to fuelMood points. Plenty of beer, wine and luxuries (every want met and stores past plentyAt x their target, full at 1.5x) lifts it by up to plentyMood. eatShare: a people short of a good buy at most that share of what's left (the rest stays on sale, dear). Mood moves moodStep points a day and is given back when the cause passes (settlement.marketMood).
markets._tuning2026_10b: Fuel and plenty retuned so they are felt (240-day surveys, seeds 101 temperate and 202 cold). Fuel: firewood holds at most 2x its target (was 4x: towns stored 80 days of wood and never felt a winter), burns 3x in the cold (was 2.5x; coal 2x), and the land yields less of it (base 0.25, forest 0.9, pasture 0.15; was 0.3/1.2/0.2). A fuel shortage (gauge > 0.1) went from 0.03% to 1.1% of town-days in the temperate world (7% of its cold days) and from 11.8% to 15.6% in the cold one. Plenty: the brewers' fill (1.25) puts beer past target after the harvest; plentyMood 2.5 (was 2). Mood > +0.25 on 22-30% of town-days, mostly autumn and winter (spring 10-20%), mean +0.1 to +0.4 with single towns up to about +1.4.
markets._trade: NPC trade (systems/marketDynamics.js): each settlement trades with its kingdom trade routes' partners and its nearest neighbours (up to `partners`, within `localRange` hexes; ports also by sea within `seaRange`). A good moves from A to B when B's scarcity beats A's by more than the haul's friction (perHex per hex, x roadFactor on a road, x seaFactor by sea). Each link carries goods worth up to `capacity` gold a day (+ perRoute per kingdom route, up to maxRoutes), at most `share` of the exporter's surplus above `keepDays` of its own need. War between the two realms, a closed blockade (sea links), a siege of either end, outlaw lairs and raiders near the road cut or thin it. The two towns keep goldScale x the value gap of what moved as trade income (Economy.processTrade).
markets._works: Works the player built or funded (market.works, systems/merchantPrince.js): after the town's own trades each runs up to its runs a day x repair x tool shortage. First it takes over a share of the runs the town's own trade made that turn: capture x the works' runs / (the works' runs + the trade's capacity) of them (the craftsmen bring their work to the better-found works: the stores are as the trade left them, only the margin goes to the works) — so a level pays where the trade is big and busy and little where it is small or idle. Then it runs on top while the town keeps `keep` of its target of every input, the output stays under `fill` x its target, and a run still adds `minMargin` of its output's worth at today's stock (the town's own scarcity curve: a glut of the output or a dearth of the input stops it). `steps`: price checks per turn. lootDamage: share of a raid's or sack's take knocked off the works' repair.
markets._ui: Labels for stock levels by scarcity (ascending).

merchantCaravans._comment: Merchant caravans and trading ships (systems/merchantCaravans.js): a sampled share of the NPC trade flows (world/settlementMarket.js) travels the map as real units whose cargo lands only when they arrive. cap: concurrent traders (perSettlement x settlements, clamped). spawn: how many links a market turn may embody and the least cargo worth a caravan (minValue, gold at base price; smaller lots land at once). land/sea: unit stats (speed in hexes a day, roadSpeed on a road the whole way; guards = base + value x perValue). purse: coin the merchant carries (share of cargo value). trade: the player's buy markup and sell markdown on the cargo price (origin value toward destination value as the journey goes). escort: pay (share of cargo value), how near the player must ride (range), how far before the merchant gives up on them (leash, for graceDays), the counsel radius. ambush: interception radius of raiders and lairs, lair odds, a realm at war seizing traders in its land, the patrol radius that helps the guards. fear: days a road stays shunned after a caravan is taken and the share of its trade it loses. robbery: realm reputation, witnesses. tolls: share of cargo value paid to a realm whose border a trader crosses. patrols: realms with full treasuries or lawful lords riding the busy roads (upkeep from the treasury). notableValue: losses worth a herald's cry.

merchantPrince._doc: Merchant Prince play (systems/merchantPrince.js, systems/marketFairs.js): the player's levers on the settlement goods economy (world/settlementMarket.js, data/markets.json). Industry: fund works in a town (mill, bakery, brewery, smithy, weaver...), keyed to the local industry recipes of data/markets.json; the works run in the town's market after its own trades and pay the investor a share of the value they add, at the town's own prices. Warehouses: rent store-rooms in a town to keep goods outside the packs, to sell into that town's market later. Forward contracts: promise a town N units by day D at a price fixed today. Fairs: seasonal fairs at the great towns, where merchants from afar bring stock and the stalls deal closer. News: heralds cry harvest gluts and dearths. Balance: docs/economy-balance.md, 'Merchant Prince'.

industry._doc: kinds: one per recipe id of data/markets.json (the trade must exist in the town: minType). The forge (iron + firewood) adds no value at base prices and the chandlery's rock oil is too rare, so neither is offered. Prices are set so a level repays itself in about 45 days in one of the great towns (docs/economy-balance.md); the weaving shed and the smithy are starved of wool and iron unless you bring them in. runsPerLevel: runs a day each level adds (at full repair; works run on market day, tickDays at once). gold and materials (from your packs) per level; each level after the first costs levelCost x more gold. maxLevel per works. investorShare: share of the value added paid to a foreign investor (the guild and the town keep the rest); out of it the investor pays the hands the works hire at the town's craft wage (data/labour.json works.hands, world/townLabour.js), some of them even while the works idle; ownShare in a town you rule (your holdings), where you also build at ownCost x the price and pay no tithe. Value added = what the run's output is worth at the town's stock less its inputs (SettlementMarket scarcity curve, before season and markup).

kinds._chandler: Guild-only works (systems/guilds.js): only a master (guildRank 2) of the town's Chandlers' Guild may fund a chandlery.

industry._tithe: The crown's cut of a foreign investor's share: base, more while the realm is at war, more again while its treasury is in crisis (data/finance.json crowns). None in a realm you rule or a town you hold. While your own court enforces 'Merchant charters' (systems/kingship.js edicts), foreign crowns honour your charters: chartersMult x the tithe.
industry._seizure: A realm at war with you (or with the realm you are sworn to) seizes your works at once. A crown in financial crisis may seize them: crisisChance a week per works. If your reputation in the realm stays below expropriateBelow for graceDays the town expropriates them (warnBelow raises a counsel warning). Seized works keep running for their new owner.
industry._damage: A raid or sack that loots the town's stores knocks lootDamage (data/markets.json works) x the loot share off the works' repair; a siege idles them and wears siegeWear a day; storm and quake damage to the town slows them. Repair costs repairCost x the works' gold (all levels) x the damage. Selling a stake back to the guild pays salvage x what you put in x its repair.

warehouse._doc: Rented store-rooms in a town, outside your packs. units: most goods held (all kinds together). keyFee once, rent every 7 days (unpaid twice running: the landlord sells the stock off to the market and ends the lease). Goods keep better than on a stall: spoilMult x the market's spoil rate a day. Theft, rolled weekly (no dice: a hash of the day and the lease): base + guildTown where the Thieves' Guild works + perHeat x your heat in the realm + an outlaw lair within lairRadius + raiders within raiderRadius, less perGuard per point of the town watch; a guild member of guildFriendRank or more is robbed guildFriendMult as often; a town you hold ownedMult. A theft carries off loss[0]..loss[1] of the stock.

forwards._doc: Forward contracts: agree today to deliver qty units of a good the town uses by day D, paid on delivery at a unit price fixed today: what the town would pay for the lot now (Trading.saleUnitPrice, its real price curve) x (1 + premiumBase + premiumPerDay x lead days, at most premiumMax), never above buying the lot back here (Trading.saleUnitCap). qty at most maxNeedDays x the town's daily need (+ minQty). Deliver from your packs or your warehouse in the town, in parts. Missed: penaltyShare of the undelivered value is forfeit (taken from your purse) and reputation falls in the realm.

fairs._doc: Seasonal fairs (systems/marketFairs.js). On day `day` of the 120-day year each fair opens for `days` days at its sites: 'capital' (every living realm's capital), 'city' (every city). Merchants from afar bring `goods`: share x the town's target stock of each good its people use (real stock that sells, spoils and travels on like any other). While the fair is on the stalls ask `ask` x and buy at `sell` of what goods are worth (instead of 70%), never above buying them back. The heralds cry it and the tavern talks of it.

news._doc: Market news the heralds cry (data/chatter.json heralds: market_fair, market_dearth, market_glut). Checked every `every` days: the worst food dearth in the world (a town in dearth, scarcity of a staple at least dearthScarcity, at least minType), and in the harvest window (days of the year) the deepest grain glut at a city or capital (scarcity at most glutScarcity). The same town is not cried again within repeatDays.

labour._doc: Labour, classes and migration (world/townLabour.js model, ticked by systems/labour.js on each town's market day). Every settlement's people are split into five strata (settlement.labour.sh, shares of settlement.population): peasants & labourers, artisans, merchants, clergy and nobility. Each stratum has its own basket (what it buys more or less of than the average townsman), so the town's daily need of each good in data/markets.json is scaled by its class mix against the usual mix for its size (a town with its usual mix buys exactly what it did before). Peasants work the land (and carry, dig and haul), artisans the town's trades and the works the player funds, merchants its trade. Hands, jobs and the wage of each sector float with the labour market; a sector short of hands caps its output, idle hands raise crime and unrest and sour the mood. Each stratum's welfare (its basket met, work, real wage, taxes, safety, famine) draws people slowly between linked towns; war, sieges, famine and conquest drive refugees to safer neighbours, who go home when the danger passes. Balance: docs/economy-balance.md 'Labour, classes and migration'.
labour._strata: sector: the work the stratum does (land, craft, trade; none for the clergy and nobility, who live on tithes, rents and office). work: share of the stratum that works for wages (the rest are children, the old and wives at home). mobility: how readily it migrates (1 = peasants). refugeeShare: its share of a refugee column against its share at home (the nobles flee first and furthest, the poor on foot).
labour._shares: The usual class mix of a settlement of each size. A town's own mix leans from it by its peoples (settlement.peoplesEffects: crafts -> artisans, enterprise and trade -> merchants, faith -> clergy, husbandry -> peasants; each point of an effect x the weight below), by the works funded in it (worksTilt artisans per level) and a holding's workshop quarter (holdingTilt x its goods effect). The mix then drifts toward that target by `drift` a market turn; migration and refugees move it off.
labour._baskets: What each stratum buys of a good against the average townsman (1 when not listed). A town's need of a good = the market's per-capita need x (sum of share x basket) / (the same sum at its size's usual mix). Gems (2026-10 economic chronicle pass): nobles 5 (was 8), merchants 1.5 (was 2), artisans 0.8 (was 0.5) — the gem cutters' and goldsmiths' own trade buys gems too, so a town's gem need swings less with its elite; fashions at court (data/chronicle.json, e.g. jewelled finery) move it for a season. With markets.json supply gems 0.95 (was 0.8) and luxuries 0.7 (was 0.9) the jewellers' row no longer stands idle late in the game (docs/economy-balance.md).
labour._jobs: Hands each sector wants (its jobs). The trades and the counting-houses are sized by the economy the town has built up (labour.base: its population, followed baseAlpha of the way each market turn), so new artisans and merchants find no place at first and a town emptied by war is short of them until it shrinks; the land takes every newcomer while it has land to spare: land = work x the usual peasant share x the people the land can employ (landCap[type] x fertility; past it each extra mouth finds only crowdSlope of a place); craft = work x the usual artisan share x pop x (craftBase + craftUtil x how busy the town's trades ran last turn); trade = work x the usual merchant share x pop x (tradeBase + tradeAct x the turn's trade volume / (pop x tradeRef), at most tradeMax). The player's works (works.hands per level) and properties (properties.wageShare of their upkeep at the base wage) hire on top. Goods by sector: craftGoods are the craftsmen's (the rest come off the land, the mines and the woods).
labour._wages: Gold a day per hand at the usual balance of jobs and hands: base[sector] x typeMult[type]; x (jobs / hands) ^ elasticity, clamped to [min, max]; x the cost of living (the scarcity of the staples the poor buy) ^ colPow. Moves `alpha` of the way a market turn.
labour._output: A sector short of hands works less: land and mines at 1 - (1 - fill) x landSensitivity, the craftsmen's goods, the town's trades and the player's works at the craft fill. A strike idles strikeFill of the craft hands.
labour._welfare: Each stratum's welfare (0..1; about 0.87 is the ordinary lot of a town at peace with full stalls): weights x the share of its basket the market met (market.met: food, drink, fuel, clothes, luxury, tools; a want the market doesn't stock counts as missing), its work (1 - idle; the clergy and nobles take the town's), its real wage (0.5 + (wage / base wage / cost of living - 1) x 1.25; the clergy and nobles take the town's), safety (1 - danger) and the famine gauge; less taxes in a town the player rules ((rate - 0.15) x taxWeight[stratum]).
labour._danger: What makes a town unsafe (0..1, summed and capped at 1): the player's siege or a siege of a holding (siege), a town taken by another crown within conquestDays (conquest), a realm at war with a linked neighbour's (border), outlaw lairs within lairRadius (lair each, at most lairMax), raiders within raiderRadius, damage from fire, flood or sack (damage x the town's damage).
labour._mood: Happiness: (town welfare - content) x perWelfare, less (idle - idleFree) x perIdle points, clamped to [min, max]; moves step points a day and is given back when the cause passes (settlement.labourMood).
labour._crime: Crime (0..1, a moving average): idle hands past idleFree x perIdle, plus the poor's misery (poorLine - peasants' welfare) x perMisery. Read by the thieves' guild (jobOdds: the town's crime x jobOdds on every job's odds), warehouse thieves (theft x crime on the weekly chance) and holdings unrest (unrest x crime + idle x unrestIdle points a day).
labour._migration: Weekly (every `every` days): along each trade link, each stratum moves from the town where it fares worse to the one where it fares better when the gap beats `threshold`: rate x (gap - threshold) x the stratum's mobility of its people a week, at most maxShare of the town in all. A town the player rules (a holding or colony) with land to spare draws settlers as if its welfare were colonyPull higher. People never leave a town below minPop.
labour._refugees: Weekly: a town in danger (danger above `from`) loses rate x danger of its people a week (at most maxShare) to linked towns in less danger (below `safe`), weighted by their welfare and size. They remember home (labour.from) and returnShare of them go back each week once it is safe (danger below `safe`) again. A column of at least newsMin is cried by the heralds.
labour._strikes: Weekly: artisans whose welfare is below `below` and whose real wage is below `wageBelow` may down tools: a hash roll under (below - welfare) x chance. A strike lasts `days` days (the craft fill falls to strikeFill), not again within `gap` days. A town booms when its welfare is at least boomAt and it gained people last week; the heralds cry it at most every boomGap days.
labour._works: Hands a level of the player's works (systems/merchantPrince.js) hires from the town's artisans, paid the local craft wage for the runs the works make (a run must earn its wages as well as its margin, or the works stand idle — SettlementMarket._runWorks; idlePay of them would be kept on as a skeleton crew while the works stand idle). The wages come out of the player's share of the value added (data/merchantPrince.json investorShare / ownShare were raised to carry them).
labour._properties: The player's properties hire from the nearest town within `radius` hexes (none in the wild: they bring their own). wageShare of a property's upkeep is its wage bill at the base wage of that town; the bill floats with the local wage, and a town short of hands staffs it only as far as its fill. Properties of the craftCategories hire artisans, the rest (farms, mines, camps) peasants and labourers.
labour._news: Records kept for the heralds and the counsel (world.labour.history, at most `cap`).

guilds._doc: Town guilds (systems/guilds.js): craft guilds keyed to the industry recipes of data/markets.json and a merchants' guild in the great towns. Each lives on its settlement (settlement.guilds[id], saved with the tile): guildhall treasury, a named guildmaster, standing with the crown (-100..100), prosperity, the squeeze that drives strikes, an optional royal charter, and its market powers in its town — an outsider toll and a weekly sale cap on its goods for non-members, a price floor on the stalls' ask, a quality premium for its masters, guild rates on its inputs for journeymen. Precedence on one good in one town: a monopoly (one slot per good: the crown's by edict, a merchant house's, the player's company's or a guild's charter; a standing charter is never overridden, a crown edict fills empty slots) > the guild's own privileges > the open market. The thieves' guild is systems/underworld.js, not this.
guilds._config: tickDays: a town's guilds take their weekly turn on its slot. minRuns: the town's own trade capacity (runs a day, SettlementMarket.tradeCapacity summed over the guild's recipes) a guild needs to form; the industry is checked monthly and the guild dissolves after declineChecks checks below half of it. membersPerRun: guild members per run a day of capacity. dues: gold a member pays the guildhall a week (x prosperity). treasuryWeeks: the hall holds at most this many weeks of dues.

config._outsiderCap: Units of each guild good a non-member may sell in the town a week: needDays x the town's daily need of it, at least min.
config._floor: The guild will not let its goods go on the stalls below floor x their base ask (a scarcity floor; chartered guilds hold a higher one).
config._squeeze: Each week a guild adds up what squeezes it (wages = the cost of bread, taxes, war levies, competition) into an average; past strikeAt for `weeks` weeks running it strikes (a hash roll under strikeChance): its trades in town halt (settlement.market.idle) for `days` and the market runs short of their goods.

guilds._ranks: The membership ladder. fee: gold to enter the rank (to the guildhall), scaled by the town's size (typeFee). dues: gold a week. minDays: days at the rank below; minStanding: standing in this guild; skill: player.skills.commerce needed. toll: share of the outsider toll still paid. premium/inputs/loans/votes/protect: benefits held from this rank.
guilds._guilds: Craft guilds by the recipes of data/markets.json they work (recipes), the goods they guard in town (goods: tolled, capped, floored, premium) and buy at guild rates (inputs). minRuns: the town's own trade capacity they need. masterpiece: goods a journeyman brings (from the packs) to be made master; they go to the town's market. A guild without recipes forms by population (minPop) — the merchants'.

priceKnowledge._doc: The player's price knowledge (systems/priceKnowledge.js): what the player knows of each town's prices, and since when. Nothing is omniscient: a town's prices are known from the player's own visits (the whole market, every day they stand there), the reports of their trading company's factors and their holdings' stewards (the whole market, every reportEvery days), merchant caravans and trading ships met on the road (the goods they carry, as priced at both ends when they set out) and tavern talk bought or heard (a few goods, possibly wrong). Every quote keeps the day it was true and its source; the trade map and the Merchant's Ledger show its age. A hearsay quote (a worth, not a stall price) is turned into an asking price by the town's size (askBySize) and into what the stalls pay by sellShare. Caps keep the book small: maxTowns towns (the stalest dropped first), a price history of historySamples samples (one every historyEvery days) for the historyTowns towns visited last, and routesCap trade routes in the profit-and-loss book. spreads: the best known buy-here, sell-there margins within maxTravelDays of travel at hexesPerDay.

hinterland._doc: The Hinterland: rural production sites around the towns (world/hinterland.js, driven by systems/concessions.js on each town's market day). Every hex within `reach` of a settlement belongs to its nearest one; the best of them become the town's rural sites by their map resource (an iron, coal, gem or gold deposit, a stone outcrop, timber, salt, a fish bank, horses, cattle) or, failing one, by the land (sheep on open pasture and hills). Sites are derived from the terrain only (no RNG, no world-generation draw): old saves derive theirs on load. Each market turn a site's output (perDay x the days of the turn x its yield x the home town's land hands, world/townLabour.js) goes half to its home settlement and half to the nearest market town within marketReach (village -> town supply), where the town's trades and the player's works take it up. Deposits (deposit: true) hold a finite reserve (units, a hash of the world seed and the hex within `reserve`), drawn down by what is dug; the yield falls once less than yieldKnee of it is left (to yieldMin at the bottom) and an empty mine closes: the downstream towns go short and its miners drift away. Balance: docs/economy-balance.md 'The Hinterland'.
hinterland._hidden: Share of the hill and mountain hexes without a map resource that hide a vein the locals know of (a hash of the world seed and the hex; its kind by the terrain's prospecting weights below). 0.25 (was 0.2) since copper joined the weights: as many hidden iron and coal veins as before, plus the copper ones (no map resource makes copper: every copper mine is a vein the locals know of, or one prospecting strikes).
hinterland._resync: Days between passes that give newly founded towns their sites and re-home sites whose town is gone.
hinterland._kinds: name, icon; good: { goodId: units a day } at full yield and full hands; resource: the map resource that makes the site; terrain: land that makes it without a resource (sheep runs); priority: which sites a town works first; hands: labourers a concession hires at the town's land wage (a crown site's hands are the town's own peasants); deposit: finite reserve [min, max] units of the first good; leasable: the crown leases it as a concession.
hinterland._yield: A deposit's yield: 1 while at least `knee` of its reserve is left, then down in a line to `min` at the bottom.
hinterland._prospect: Each settlement is searched once every `every` days (on its market day): with `chance` (a hash roll) a new vein is struck. A waning deposit (less than `wane` of its reserve left) is the first place they look: it gains [veinMin, veinMax] of its first reserve. Else a new deposit is found on a hill or mountain hex within reach that is no site yet (kind by the terrain's weights below), up to `extraSites` past the town's usual count. Miners follow a strike: strikeMigrants peasants from the nearest neighbour; an exhausted mine sends exhaustMigrants x its hands to the nearest town. The player may fund a search (systems/concessions.js prospect): `cost` gold, `days` to dig, `playerChance` of a strike, and the finder's right to lease it at the reserve price for `finderDays`.
hinterland._concessions: The crown leases its deposits (leasable kinds) as concessions. A holder (the player or an NPC merchant house) pays a lease fee for the term into the realm's treasury, then a royalty on every unit dug (royalty x the good's base price), and hires the hands at the home town's land wage (they are extra land jobs there, world/townLabour.js). A concession digs `boost` x the crown's rate (better found pits), at the rate the holder sets: light, normal or hard (hard digs more, wastes more of the vein, risks accidents that kill hands and stall the pit, and sours the town). Output is sold into the market town at `sellShare` of what the lot is worth there (its scarcity curve, the haulage and the factor's cut), or delivered to the holder's works within contractRange (a store beside the works, up to binDays of its runs) . Reserve price: reserveShare of the gross value of a term's output at the market town's prices today (royalties are on base prices). Auctions: each realm puts one site up every auctionEvery days (staggered by realm) for auctionDays; houses bid a share [houseBid] of their estimate of the term's net (x their temperament's bid), at most houseMax concessions each. Arrears (wages and royalties the holder cannot pay) past graceDays forfeit the lease. War with the realm, a declared default on its lenders (systems/finance.js), or a royal edict (a crown in crisis: edictChance a week) revoke it.
hinterland._markers: Map markers: sites show from this zoom; a deposit's bar is green above `low` of its reserve left, amber above `critical`, red below.
hinterland._counsel: Counsel hints: a vein running out (yield below `yieldBelow` or less than `reserveBelow` of the reserve left), auctions within `auctionRadius` hexes.

tradePolicy._comment: Kingdom trade policy (src/systems/tradePolicy.js). Each realm keeps import and export tariffs per good category (imp/exp, shares of the goods' value), export bans, embargoes, trade treaties, retaliatory tariffs in trade wars and a state granary on kingdom.tradePolicy. Tariffs add to the friction of NPC trade between realms (world/settlementMarket.js flows) and are paid into the treasuries; caravans pay them as their border toll; the player pays them selling goods bought in another realm. NPC crowns decide on their weekly turn (turnDays, staggered by realm).
tradePolicy._policyEvery: Tariffs, treaties, rival embargoes and trade wars are weighed every policyEvery turns (monthly); hunger (export bans), war embargoes and the granary every turn.
tradePolicy._categories: Good categories the crowns tariff. Goods not listed fall in `defaultCategory`.
tradePolicy._stances: A crown's leaning: base import (imp) and export (exp) tariff, scaled per category by catMult. The stance follows a protectionism score: personality + culture + a yearly hash jitter; below `free` → free trade, above `mercantilist` → mercantilist.
tradePolicy._crisis: An empty or indebted treasury raises tariffs: × mult + add while the treasury is under treasuryBelow, the debt over debtRatio, or payments are missed.
tradePolicy._lobby: Town guilds lobby their crown for protection: + perGuild import tariff on a category for each guild in the realm guarding its goods, at most cap.
tradePolicy._ban: A crown bans the export of `category` while at least hungryShare of its towns starve (famine or market dearth), or while its food index is foodIndex × the world's (world/economyIndex.js relativeFood); lifted after minDays once none starve and the index is under liftIndex.
tradePolicy._embargo: War embargoes the enemy (lifted warLiftDays after peace once relations recover above liftAbove); a rival under rivalBelow is embargoed on a weekly roll; the other side's relations drop by `relation`; the realm's stability by `stability` while it lasts.
tradePolicy._treaty: Trading partners with relations at relationAt (or allies at allyAt) sign treaties on a weekly roll: tariffs waived both ways, the links' trade × (1 + linkBoost), relations + relation a week (to relationCap), stability + stability. Broken under breakBelow or by war.
tradePolicy._tradeWar: When a partner's tariffs on a realm's goods exceed its own by margin, the realm retaliates (step more on that partner's goods, to cap); each step costs relations and stability. Calm (relations above calmAbove, or the partner backs down) eases it by decay a week.
tradePolicy._granary: State granaries: a realm with minTreasury buys grain where it is in glut (scarcity under buyBelow, buyShare of the surplus, maxBuy a town a week, in at most maxTowns towns) up to capPerHead × its people, and releases it in hungry towns (releaseDays of their need, maxRelease a town a week). spoil: share lost a week.
tradePolicy._player: The player as a merchant. Goods bought in a realm are booked by origin; sold in another realm they pay its import tariff (licence: none). Goods from a realm the seller's realm embargoes can't be sold openly — smuggle them (catch odds, heat, fines). Selling abroad goods whose export the origin crown bans is a breach: heat there per unit. A licence (petitioned from a crown) waives its tariffs and bans for `days`. Brokering a treaty between two realms costs gifts and earns prestige.
tradePolicy._ruler: The realm the player rules: tariff levels to choose from; the Guild Coalition (merchants faction) shifts by perTariff × the change (cut tariffs please them), lobbyPlease for protecting a lobbied category, and for embargoes, treaties, bans and the granary.

harvests._doc: Harvests & the agricultural year (world/harvests.js). Each year every region (a realm's land, or for free towns a zone of zoneCell hexes) grows a harvest. Through the growing season (doy 1..settleDay) the weather at up to samplePoints of its largest towns is sampled every sampleEvery days and scored against the place's own climate normal (the mean of the same days over normalYears calendar years: the weather is a pure function of the hex and the day), so a dry year in a desert is a bad year, not every year. War on the region's land (each war the realm fights, each battle fought on it, raiders and war hosts abroad on it), blights (hash-rolled per region and year, spreading to neighbouring regions) and short land hands cut it. On settleDay the harvest is reckoned; it scales the region's towns' grain, wine, linen and livestock output (and the player's farms) until the next one: the seasonal curve keeps its shape, the harvest sets its amplitude. Tuned against kingdom survival (seeds 7-16) in docs/economy-balance.md 'Harvests'.
harvests._growing: The growing season: weather, war and blights count from sowDay to settleDay (days of the year); the harvest is reckoned on settleDay (a market-profile boundary: the towns' output turns over that day).
harvests._zoneCell: Towns outside any realm share a harvest region per cell of [q, r] hexes.
harvests._neighbourRange: Regions are neighbours (blights spread between them) when any two of their towns lie within this many hexes.
harvests._weather: Score per sampled day by weather type (storms count summerStorm x in summer: they lay the ripening crop flat). The season's mean score against the climate normal sets the weather yield 1 + gain x (mean - normal), clamped to [min, max].
harvests._war: Share of the crop lost to war, summed over the season: perWar per war the realm fights (levies off the land, foragers), perBattle per pitched battle fought on its land, perRaider per raider or war host abroad on it (averaged over the samples); at most max. A sacked town (settlement.damage) loses damage x townDamage of its own crop.
harvests._labour: A town whose land hands (world/townLabour.js) fill less than `below` of the jobs at harvest loses (below - fill) x k of its crop in the fields.
harvests._blights: Hash-rolled once per region and year: with `chance` a blight starts on a day in `start` (days of the year) and takes `severity` of the crops it `hits` (grain, veg, fibre, vine, fodder; stock = the herds: meat, cheese, hides, wool, horses). warmAbove: only where the region's mean temperature exceeds it. Each sample day an active blight may cross to a neighbouring region (spread a month, scaled to the sample interval), at decay x its severity.
harvests._crops: A town's farmland splits into grain, veg (vegetables and legumes), fibre (flax), vine (vineyards and orchards) and fallow (and the hay and grazing on it). The climate sets each crop's weight (climate: base weight, x the factors where the land fits); each sowing the mix drifts `drift` of the way toward the climate weights x the town's prices (scarcity ^ elasticity: grain and veg follow grain, fibre textiles, vine wine, fallow meat and cheese). Thin soil makes the farmers rest more land (fallow x (1 + (1 - soil) x soilFallow)). veg is hardier: it feels vegDamp of the weather's swing; vegFood: veg as grain for the market.

crops._temperature: Tile temperature bands for the climate factors: cool below cool, warm above warm, hot above hot, cold below cold (mild otherwise for vines).

harvests._soil: Soil condition (1 = sound). Each sowing it moves `rate` of the way toward 1 + k x (rest - rest0) (rest = fallow + half the veg: legumes feed the soil; rest0 = the climate's usual), within [min, max]. Every crop's yield is x soil.
harvests._effects: How a harvest reaches the economy. grain: the town's market grain x (grain x yield + veg x vegFood x veg yield) / the same at its first mix, within [grainMin, grainMax]; econShare of that swing reaches the granary food the people eat (world/economy.js). wine x vine share x yield / its first, x (first vine / usual vine) ^ wineClimate (warm lands make more). linen: flax adds textiles (linen) = need x linen x fibre share / the usual x yield. Livestock goods x herds' yield x (1 + fodder x (fallow - first fallow)). rentShare of the swing reaches the tithe and rents of the player's holdings (Taxation.collectTaxes). The hinterland's sheep runs, ranches and studs follow the herds' yield.
harvests._rotations: The player's farms choose a rotation: yield x their output, soil the target their soil drifts toward (rate as above) each harvest.

intensive.label: Intensive (no fallow)
intensive.note: Every field sown every year: more now, thinner soil later.

three_field.label: Three-field rotation
three_field.note: Winter grain, spring legumes, a field at rest: the old way.

rest.label: Long fallow
rest.note: Half the land rests under clover and sheep: less now, rich soil later.

harvests._propertyCrops: Which harvest a player property follows (others are not harvests). Irrigated land feels irrigatedDamp of a bad year.
harvests._herdSites: Hinterland site kinds (data/hinterland.json) that are herds: their output follows the herds' yield at their home town.
harvests._forecast: The coming harvest becomes known as the season goes: the estimate is 1 + (the weather so far - 1) x the share of the season sampled, x the war and blights so far. Players learn their own region's estimate where they stand, and every region's at a market town's weekly crop report (from reportFrom, every reportEvery days). The heralds cry a failing harvest (estimate below failingBelow from heraldFrom), a bumper one (above bumperAbove from bumperFrom) and every blight; townsfolk talk of them (tavern `harvest` condition) from talkFrom to talkUntil (the reckoned harvest after settleDay).
harvests._counsel: The Steward points at a known failing harvest (estimate below failingBelow) within radius hexes from failingFrom to failingUntil (days of the year), and at the player's farms whose soil is below soilBelow.
harvests._famine: The lean months after a failed harvest: on `day` (of the year) a realm whose harvest came in below `below` falls into the Hungry Months (worldEvents.json `event`) with chance (below - yield) x perPoint, at most max (a hash roll; the event's own dice come from a stream seeded by it, not the game's).

chronicle._doc: The Economic Chronicle: the player's unified ledger (systems/ledger.js), the realms' weekly economic indices (world/economyIndex.js), the gazette the player reads in market towns and their net worth (systems/economyChronicle.js), and fashions that move the nobles' and merchants' baskets (world/fashions.js). Nothing here draws RNG: fashions start on a hash of the world seed and the week.
chronicle._ledger: Every gold flow the player has, by source. A system reports a flow with Ledger.record(player, category, signed amount); the day's flows close into player.financeHistory (one row a day, the last `days` days). kind: 'op' counts in the income statement (earned or spent running your affairs), 'cap' is capital and stock (goods bought and sold, works and properties bought, loan principal: shown apart, not as profit or loss), 'memo' is paid inside a price (a guild's toll on what you sold: shown as 'of which', never summed). Trading margins (stalls, portTrade, storeRooms, forwards, caravanTrade) are each sale against the average cost of the good bought (systems/priceKnowledge.js). Categories not listed count as 'op' in the 'other' group.

guildTolls.name: Guild tolls in your sale prices

saleDuties.name: Import duties in your sale prices

bills.name: Bills of exchange drawn and paid

chronicle._netWorth: Net worth = gold + bank deposits + royal bonds + goods (packs, holds, store-rooms) at the best price your book knows the stalls pay (base x goodsShare when unknown) + book value of properties (their cost, losing propertyDepreciation a year down to propertyFloor), works (what you put in x their repair), ships (their value x shipShare) and your trading company - loans owed and rent in arrears. Sampled weekly (worthWeeks samples).
chronicle._indices: Each realm's economy, measured every `every` days over its settlements (population-weighted) and for the whole world, kept for historyWeeks samples: food = what the food goods cost against their base price (100 = base; season, scarcity and debased coin all count), goods = the same over every market good weighted by what people spend on it, trade = goods moved by merchants in a market turn, shortages = towns short of something (scarcity at least shortageAt), dearth = towns in food dearth, idle = share of hands without work, welfare = how content the people are, treasury, debt ratio and coin purity. changeWeeks: the 'since' comparison for inflation. News for the heralds: a realm's food index at least dearAt, at least dearRel times the world's and up at least surgePct since changeWeeks ago (the lean weeks alone are no news), or its goods index up inflationPct and inflationRel more than the world's (a debased coin shows here; each realm at most once per newsGapWeeks). Readers, on the realm's food against the world's: KingdomStability's target ('Cost of living': dearer than dearFrom costs perPoint a point up to stability.max, cheaper than plentyBelow gives stability.plenty) and KingdomAI.considerWar (dearer than war.dearFrom lowers a crown's confidence, at most war.max).
chronicle._gazette: Realm-level indices are public: a gazette is posted weekly in every settlement with a market. Standing in one, the player reads it: their own realm's latest numbers and the other realms' a week older (news travels), the world's, and the fashions within gazetteRadius hexes. Town-level prices stay what the price book knows (systems/priceKnowledge.js).
chronicle._fashions: Fashions at court (world/fashions.js): every `every` days, while fewer than maxActive run and from minDay, a fashion starts at a living realm's capital with startChance (a hash of the world seed and the week). It spreads outward speed hexes a day up to maxRadius, rising over `rise` days, holding `hold` days and fading over `fade` days, weaker with distance (falloff). While it holds a town, the strata listed (with their weight) want more (or less) of its goods: goods a market keeps change the town's need of them (TownLabour.demandMults), so prices move with the stock; goods no market keeps (exotics, silk, ivory) sell for more at the stalls and ports (x the same factor). Players with standing can set one (playerSet): at a capital where their reputation is at least minReputation (or a realm they rule), for prestige House Prestige and gold, halved with an artist or architect client in their pay, at most once every cooldown days; their fashion is `power` times as strong and lasts `longer` times as long.

bourse._comment: Underwriters, bills of exchange and the Bourse (src/systems/underwriting.js, src/systems/bills.js, src/systems/bourse.js). Balance notes in docs/economy-balance.md; the rules in GAMEPLAY_MANUAL.md → 'Underwriters, Bills & the Bourse'.

underwriting._cover: Open cover: one standing policy per kind, bought at an underwriter's office. Each day it bills a premium on what it covers that day (ships at sea, caravans on the road, stock in store, works, farms): the expected loss from the same inputs the loss sites use, times `loading`, times the claims surcharge. It attaches `attachDays` after it is opened and pays each covered loss less the deductible, up to `maxClaim` a loss.

marine.name: Hull & cargo
marine._risk: Per day at sea. Storms: the season's chance of foul weather at sea × the hull damage (in repair cost) and cargo washed overboard they bring. Hostile squadrons near the ship: their chance of stopping it × the chance it loses × hull damage and cargo seized. Events at sea (on a voyage): ships.json's eventChance a day × the share of events that batter the hull (eventHullShare, eventHullPct) or put cargo over the side (eventCargoShare × eventCargoLoss). stormChance is the season's expected storm danger at sea (measured: storms and blizzards, weighted by their seaDanger). A worn hull (below ships.json settings.leakBelow, 50%) leaks: storms wash more cargo out of it.

caravan.name: Goods on the road
caravan._risk: Per caravan per day: base, plus perRaider for each raider within raiderRadius of it and perLair for each outlaw lair within lairRadius; halved on a road-linked journey (wardens). Covers your caravans and your company's convoys.

stock.name: Stock in store
stock._risk: Each store-room's and post's own weekly theft chance (MerchantPrince.theftChance, MerchantHouses.robberyChance) × the share thieves carry off × the stock's value, billed by the day.

works.name: Works & property
works._risk: Per works per day: base × its value; a siege wears siegeWear a day (the repair bill); a crown in crisis may seize it (crisisChance a week × the salvage value). Seizure by a realm at war with you is a war risk no underwriter covers; neither is a town turning on you.

crop.name: Crops in the field
crop._risk: Per farm per day: the day's expected crop × the season's expected shortfall to weather (`seasonShortfall`) plus any blight or drought on the land now. A field with a worse record of its own (an average of its days, experienceWeight) is priced on that instead. Pays the shortfall of each day's crop against what the farm would bring in fair weather.
crop._harvest: The year's harvest (world/harvests.js): through the growing season (harvests.json → growing) each day bills the expected shortfall of the farm's region over the season's length × the farm's yearly crop — the forecast's shortfall as far as it is sure (conf), harvestPrior (a usual year's expected shortfall) where it is not. When the harvest is reckoned, the region's shortfall in the farm's crop × its yearly crop is claimed, pro rata to the days of the season the cover carried.

guild._doc: Underwriters' guilds at the great ports: their own capital pool. A guild whose capital falls below failBelow of what it started with fails: its covers lapse and its claims are paid at `recovery`. A new guild opens `refoundDays` later.

book._doc: Each underwriter also writes covers for other merchants. Every week its book earns premium (premium × book) and pays claims: lossRatio of the premium in quiet times, more for each war, blockade, pirate fleet and great storm in its waters (warLoss, blockadeLoss, pirateLoss), with noise. A banking house's desk books it all on the house's reserves (systems/finance.js); a guild on its own capital.

fraud._doc: A false claim: forged protests of loss bought through the Thieves' Guild (rank minRank or above). The forger takes forgerFee of the claim at once. Every false claim is investigated: caught with `caught` chance, less perRank for each guild rank, more perClaim for each claim of yours in the last claimsMemoryDays and bigShare for a claim near the cap. Caught: no pay, the cover is cancelled, a fine of fineMult × the claim (from your purse; what you cannot pay becomes heat), heat in the realm, the office will not insure you for banDays.

bills._doc: Bills of exchange: pay gold into one banking house and draw a bill payable at another house (or the same house's seat in another realm). fee = base + perHex × the distance between the two seats, min minFee; payable from usance days (the distance at usanceHexes a day); presented after validDays it is protested (protestFee). A thief who takes a bill can have it cashed by a forger after cashDays unless you stop it at a branch of the paying house first (stopFee). A bill on a failed house falls on the house that drew it; if that one failed too, the receivers pay `recovery`.

bourse._doc: The Bourse: an exchange in each of the `exchanges` greatest capitals. Shares in the rival merchant houses (100 each), the banking houses (1000), the player's company once floated (100) and the chartered companies (ventures and royal monopolies, 1000). Each share's fair value is its earnings over the yield the market asks of its kind (see _yields); a bank's is weighed by its vaults (reserveWeight); its price is fair × sentiment (a mean-reverting walk) × the market's mood × any mania, and the player's own trading moves it (impact, decaying by the day). Dividends are paid weekly from real profit.
bourse._yields: The yield the market asks of each kind: a share is worth its book × (1 + slope × (return on capital ÷ yield − 1)), the return a running average weighted roeWeight a week, within [minMult, maxMult] of book: 1× book at the yield asked, more above it, damped by the kind's slope (the market is wary of paying up front for growth). `priors` is the return each kind is expected to make before it has shown any: a merchant house's mining leases (systems/concessions.js) make its trade worth far more than its books.

ventures.name: The Company of the Far Isles
ventures._doc: An overseas venture under a crown's charter: it lives by new lands (Discovery: sites found and known to its crown, colonies claimed) and dies by the sea (pirates, war, a fleet lost).

ventures.name: The Royal {good} Farm of {kingdom}
ventures._doc: A crown's monopoly let to a company: its rents follow the realm's trade and prices (world/economyIndex.js); a crown deep in debt squeezes it, a crown that defaults may revoke it.

panics._doc: Market-wide falls in mood: a banking house failing, a crown defaulting or a war on an exchange's realm.

meta.description: LPC terrain spritesheet — tile classification and mapping
meta.note: The terrain sheets are 512x832 = 16cols x 26rows of 32x32 tiles. Tiles are organized into autotile transition groups. This file separates FILL tiles (uniform solid ground) from EDGE tiles (transition/corner tiles that blend two terrains). Only tiles in 'fills' should be used for ground rendering.

_note: Documents the spritesheet's autotile transition groups.
Each terrain type occupies a 6-col x 3-row block:
Additional 3x3 blocks at cols 6-8, 9-11 are TRANSITION BLENDS
between two terrain types — these contain mixed-color edge tiles.
The center tile of a transition blend IS the target terrain fill.
FILL  = fully opaque, uniform color (stddev < 8) — safe for ground
TXTR  = fully opaque, textured (stddev >= 8) — may be fill or edge
TRANS = partially transparent — definitely an edge/overlay tile
